News.content:
The Alpine Club said a ground team would take the recovered bodies to a Japanese camp.

Prior to Purja's death being announced, Pakistani officials said the bodies of three other climbers from his expedition - American Mallory Geis, Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy from Oman and Pur Bahadur Gurung from Nepal - had been recovered.

On Saturday, Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah said "the tragic death of six Nepalese and four other foreign climbers, including world record holder Nirmal Purja, in the Karakoram mountain range of Pakistan, has shocked us".

"The history of their courage, dedication, and contributions will always remain inspiring," the prime minister added.

In a statement, Purja's older brother Kamal wrote: "It is with the heaviest heart that I share the devastating news that my beloved younger brother, Nirmal 'Nimsdai' Purja, and the other climbers are no longer with us.

"Although our hearts are broken, we are incredibly proud of you. Your legacy will live forever," he added.

Prince William said he was "truly saddened to hear of the tragic death" of Purja, who he said "served with distinction" as a soldier before "becoming one of the greatest mountaineers".

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a post on X: "Incredibly sad to learn of the passing of Nirmal (Nims) Purja and those he was climbing with.

"He was an inspirational man who served in our Armed Forces for many years - and whose incredible mountaineering adventures are known the world over."

Naila Kiani, a spokesperson for the Alpine Club of Pakistan which is involved in the rescue efforts, told BBC's Newshour programme on Saturday that her organisation feared all members of the group were dead, and that Purja had led many expeditions she was on.

Praising his leadership skills, she described him as a "very experienced climber and fearless".

Teams in Pakistan have been searching for the climbers on the world's 12th-highest summit since Thursday's avalanche on the 8,047m (26,400ft) peak in the Karakoram range.

The multinational climbing group was being led by Purja. Also known as Nims, he rose to prominence in 2019 when he climbed all 14 of the world's mountains with peaks above 8,000m in 189 days - smashing the previous record by more than seven years.

He became widely known following a Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible, released two years later.

At the time, he said: "It has been a gruelling but humbling six months, and I hope to have proven that anything is possible with some determination, self-belief and positivity."

Purja served in the British military for 16 years, 10 of which were spent in the special forces, and he was awarded an MBE by the late Queen in 2018 for his achievement in extreme high-altitude mountaineering.

Purja, who lived with his wife and three-year-old daughter in Hampshire in southern England, said he was also the first Gurkha to climb Everest while serving in the British military.

In his last post on X, published on Monday, he said he had not intended to climb Broad Peak.

"Initially, the plan was to climb just G2," Purja wrote, referring to Gasherbrum II, another peak in the Karakoram mountain range.

But right before he set off for Pakistan, he realised if he also managed to climb Broad Peak while he was there, he would have only one more mountain to conquer before becoming the "first person in history to climb all 14 eight-thousanders twice. Without oxygen."

An eight-thousander is a mountain that rises more than 8,000m above sea level.

"This wasn't planned," Purja wrote. "But opportunities don't scream: they whisper to those already working in silence."

"Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down. I take zero mountains for granted," he wrote.

Broad Peak is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for climbers. The first successful ascent was in 1957, when an Austrian expedition reached the summit.

Since then, many more have climbed the mountain, but dozens have lost their lives.

One of Broad Peak's deadliest years was 2013, when at least six fatalities were recorded.

News.title: Why I don't regret choosing a vasectomy in my 20s
News.content:
Because he was asking for a vasectomy at such a young age, Sam had prepared for the questions his doctor was going to ask him: Don't you think you're too young to know you don't want kids? Could you change your mind in future? You do know reversals are expensive and aren't always successful?

"[The doctor] actually said he had very recently changed his view," says Sam. "And that, if I had come in half a year earlier, he would have turned me away instantly."

His vasectomy took place a couple of months after he first contacted the clinic.

The questions from Sam's doctor were designed to ensure he was making a decision he could live with; men under 30 are more likely to regret a vasectomy, according to guidance from NHS Scotland, external.

Dr Sarah Salkeld, a former GP who is now a medical director for MSI Reproductive Choices, a group of clinics offering various contraceptives to NHS and private patients, says a vasectomy is "very safe and effective".

But she cautions it is important for men to "really think about" whether a vasectomy is right for them.

"We offer everyone counselling to talk about it if they want to, just toâ¦ make sure they've got all the information they need to make that decision."

She says reversals are not routinely available on the NHS as there are strict criteria for having one.

The NHS website points out that other forms of contraception, external are available to men, including condoms and the fertility awareness method - avoiding sex or using condoms on the days when their female partner is most fertile.

Sam told his doctor that, while he loved kids and had a happy childhood himself, he wanted to stay focused on his job as a sound designer for video games.

News.title: Love Island has a problem, say fans - 'there hasn't been much love'
News.content:
What's your dream Love Island series on paper?

Some watch for the heartwarming romances, like Molly-Mae Hague and Tommy Fury falling for each other back in 2019, while others prefer intense dramas - we see you 2022 winners Ekin-Su CÃ¼lcÃ¼loÄlu and Davide Sanclimenti.

Others tune in for exciting challenges like Snog, Marry, Pie or the ones which literally send heart rates soaring.

For most, it's a mix of all of the above, and it's a balance TV producers have been trying to strike for years with the original UK series, as well as a host of spin-offs and international editions.

It's no secret that Love Island UK linear viewing figures have dropped from their 2019 heyday, with streaming and social media becoming more of a focus.

Across the pond the US edition has been reaching new heights, with the latest eighth series ranked as the number one reality show for five weeks in the States across all streaming platforms, according to its streamer Peacock. , external

It also had an injection of star power as US celebrity fans, including Lizzo, Demi Lovato and Kesha, sent messages of support to the finalists, while rapper Megan Thee Stallion has become a regular guest.

BBC Newsbeat has been speaking to fans, commentators and an ex-Islander to see what they feel the UK edition could learn from the US version to regain its spark.

News.title: Solitude as a new aspirational lifestyle: 'We are not lonely'
News.content:
It's a Friday night. A young woman trudges back to her apartment after a day of work. She enters a spotless kitchen, unloads a bag of groceries, and unwraps a frozen pizza before sliding it in the oven.

What follows is a nightly routine that is almost meditative in its mundanity: she lights a candle and gazes briefly at the snow-covered landscape outside her window, piles a premade salad onto a plate with the pizza, and settles on her sofa to eat in front of the TV.

The tagline that accompanies the scene reads: "POV you're a childfree and single girl that has no friends and lives alone so this is how you spend your Friday night."

At the centre of the video â which has amassed seven million views on TikTok â is Lana Isa, a software sales manager in her 20s based in Toronto.

In addition to chronicling her nightly self-care routines, she takes her almost 400,000 followers across TikTok and Instagram on late-night fast food drives, reading sessions perched on a rock by the lake, even a saga of getting locked out of her apartment in the middle of the night.

Isa is part of a growing, albeit niche corner of the internet where content creators, many of them women, share their daily rituals of living alone, choosing to spotlight a lifestyle that prioritises peace and solitude - the antithesis of social media excess.

For Isa, unveiling the "no friends" aspect of her life was less of a tagline, but the "reality" she had been living for several years.

News.title: Spider-Man fans hail Brand New Day as Holland's best yet
News.content:
Fans have been queuing outside cinemas to catch the latest Spider-Man film, with many hailing it as a spectacular return for the web-slinging superhero.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day marks Tom Holland's fourth standalone adventure as the protagonist and hero Peter Parker.

Picking up after the events of Spider-Man: No Way Home, the film follows Parker as he devotes his time to protecting New York City while adjusting to a life in which everyone, including his closest friends, has forgotten who he is.

The fourth Spider-Man film is director Destin Daniel Cretton's second project in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), having previously been at the helm of Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings.

Appearing together in the same film for a second time this summer, Holland reprises the role alongside his wife Zendaya, who stars once again as MJ.

There is also a return for Jon Bernthal's Punisher, making his first appearance in an MCU feature film, and an introduction to the MCU for Sadie Sink, whose role in the plot has been kept firmly under wraps.

News.title: Peak District's rebrand deal brings in cash but also criticism
News.content:
A deal between Peak District bosses and car firm Skoda to put up temporary signs welcoming tourists to "the Peaq District" in honour of the firm's new electric model has given the park authority's coffers a welcome boost.

However, it has also sparked protests from campaigners and residents unhappy about the commercial aspect of the arrangement.

One campaigner said: "If national parks are prepared to sell their very name to the highest bidder, then we're already on the path to industrial extraction of the most protected landscapes."

Park bosses have defended the "fantastic" deal and said the partnership brought in extra funds for conservation and heritage work.

With national parks continuing to grapple with funding pressures, could the partnership be a sign of things to come for the Peak District and beyond?

News.title: Ginger hair portraits show unexpected 'golden thread' connecting Americans
News.content:
For Kieran Dodds, photographing people with red hair has become something of an obsession over the past decade.

The 45-year-old, from Edinburgh, who is himself a "proud ginger", began taking pictures in his homeland in 2013 as part of a series examining Scottish identity.

His interest in the subject soon took him to other ginger hotspots such the Russian city of Perm and Jamaica's Treasure Beach.

His 2020 book Gingers spanned the world but after its release he notice there was a "huge gap".

"I realised I didn't have any American citizens," Kieran told the BBC.

"Then all these people got in touch."

News.title: Trust, grief and betrayal: Inside the Legacy funeral case
News.content:
This story contains details some might find distressing.

I've reported on many criminal cases before, but nothing like that of undertaker Robert Bush.

Now the case is over, we can report on what it was like to follow a story that began when whistleblowers raised concerns about Legacy Independent Funeral Directors with Humberside Police in March 2024.

Bush, the former owner of Legacy in Hull, admitted 67 offences, including fraudulent trading, denying 30 people a decent and proper burial, and giving some bereaved relatives the ashes of strangers.

The scale of Bush's offending was extraordinary. Police identified 300 victims.

Some were families who had paid Bush for funeral plans and services.

Others were relatives left questioning whether the ashes they had received really belonged to their loved ones.

There were also the deceased, whose bodies he had been trusted to bury or cremate with dignity.

Bush's scores of victims meant seats in courtroom four at Hull Crown Court for his five-day sentencing were in high demand.

Every day, diligent ushers stood like bouncers at the court's heavy, soundproof doors. They ensured families were given priority to see the man who wronged their loved ones face justice.

Court staff escorted them in with boxes of tissues, paper cups of water and a kind hand on their arms. Some were wiping away tears before they even walked into the room.

Fearful of what they were about to hear.

Their worries were not misplaced. The details of Bush's crimes were harrowing.

Among them, discarding stillborn premature baby Sunny Beverley-Conlin on the floor in a paper bag, and abandoning one victim naked on the floor to "let nature take its course".

They are descriptions one grieving mother said "will never leave me".

News.title: Son of Wicker Man maker dies just weeks before his sequel to film premieres
News.content:
British filmmaker Justin Hardy, who directed a sequel to his late father Robin's 1973 cult horror classic The Wicker Man, has died aged 61.

His family said Hardy died on Friday night after suffering a heart attack, remembering him as "a man of family, of boundless creativity" and "so full of life right to the end".

A Bafta and Emmy nominated writer and director, Hardy was known for the documentary Children of the Wicker Man in 2024, made with his brother Dominic, which chronicled the legacy of their father's iconic film.

He had just completed production on Wrath of the Gods, the concluding chapter to the Wicker Man trilogy, which was due to premiere in London later this month.

Hardy also directed historical films and documentaries for the BBC, Channel 4 and CNN, including Princes In The Tower, Trafalgar Battle Surgeon, The Relief Of Belsen and Spanish Flu: The Forgotten Fallen.

His family said they were "devastated" by his death and "heartbroken" Hardy would not be able to see Wrath of the Gods open.

Dominic described his brother as having "an incredible appetite for life".

"We've lost him and we've lost that larger-than-life presence looking over us all," he said. "He really became a filmmaker his own right."

Dominic also praised Hardy's work on his last film as "incredibly beautiful", adding it was "a great satisfaction to him" to have made something new.

The Wicker Man, starring Edward Woodward and Christopher Lee, is the story of a police officer sent to a remote Scottish island community to investigate the disappearance of a local girl.

Wrath of the Gods was inspired by recently discovered scripts and storyboards by Hardy's late father Robin, marking the end of the trilogy that began with The Wicker Man and the 2011 follow-up The Wicker Tree.

Hardy, who also taught screenwriting at University College London, is survived by his wife Larissa, and their four children.

News.title: The legacy of Epping's asylum protests a year on: 'It's still discussed in shops, pubs and cafes'
News.content:
When Anita bought her house in the upmarket town of Epping, she dreamed of a happy retirement enjoying the nature surrounding her.

What she did not bargain for was her Essex home becoming a battleground of anti-asylum seeker protests and counter-demonstrations in July 2025.

It followed the arrest of Ethiopian migrant Hadush Kebatu, who was living at The Bell Hotel in the town when he sexually assaulted a schoolgirl and a woman.

Most protests that followed were peaceful - and protesters argue they were a force for good. However, some descended into chaos and six people have been jailed for violent disorder so far.

At one point, Epping Forest District Council considered evacuating nearby houses due to the chaos.

The case sparked a wider conversation about the effect of housing asylum seekers in hotels in British communities.

"Overnight, our local social media platforms went from people seeking lost cats to the most vitriolic, horrible things," recalls Anita.

Like others in this story, she does not want her full name used for fear of being targeted.

News.title: Cambridge professor at centre of plagiarism row defends his work
News.content:
A Cambridge University professor has defended his academic work after finding himself at the centre of a plagiarism row.

The row erupted after another academic - self-defined "race realist" Nathan Cofnas, who was sacked from his Cambridge role in 2024 - said he found numerous instances of plagiarism in Prof Jason Arday's work and questioned some of his stated achievements.

While some critics say the treatment of Arday, who is black, has been motivated by racism, others have said the claims of plagiarism were legitimate.

Arday admitted errors in his work, telling the Times, external in an interview on Saturday that he was accountable for those mistakes but that "what I am not is a liar".

He told the newspaper: "There has been, since I arrived at Cambridge, a very well orchestrated and co-ordinated campaign to unseat me from my position."

He argued this was "racially motivated" and that he had become a "lightning rod" for criticism of diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) policy.

Arday said some errors in his early academic work was because of his autism, as he relied on using mimicry to make sense of information, and that similar scrutiny would find similar errors in work by other academics.

"We're talking about academia here. I didn't murder somebody. I think the cruelty that I've experienced and the positioning of me as this kind of liar and fantasist is totally unacceptable," he told the newspaper.

In 2023, the then 37-year-old sociologist became the youngest ever black professor at Cambridge, telling the BBC at the time his work focused on neurodivergence and race in education.

He was diagnosed with autism and global development delay in his early years, to which his being unable to speak until the age of 11 and unable to read or write until 18 was attributed.

Arday worked as a PE teacher before earning his doctorate at Liverpool John Moores University and going on to teach at Roehampton, Durham and Glasgow.

News.title: Ballot paper for Clacton by-election is longest in British electoral history
News.content:
The longest ballot paper in British political history is costing four times as much to print than regular ballot papers, the local council has said.

The list for the Clacton parliamentary by-election, which was prompted by the resignation of Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, is 90cm (3ft) long.

When people unfold the paper, they will find it is longer than most adults' arms.

Tendring District Council chief executive Ian Davidson - who is the acting returning officer for the by-election in the Essex constituency - said organising the vote had been "manic".

People have already started returning postal votes to town hall and most registered voters will go to polling stations on 13 August.

Davidson said: "We've logistically been looking at the size of the ballot paper, how we fold it to get it into the envelope so we can send it out to our postal voters [and] how we manage the polling stations."

News.title: Emotional Kerr delivers moment Glasgow 2026 has waited for with men's mile gold
News.content:
There were no pacers. No wave lights. No declarations about what time he would run or what record he would beat. This was a Saturday night scrap - Glasgow rules - and Josh Kerr wasn't going to let anyone beat him in that fight.

Not his childhood pal and Scotland team-mate Jake Wightman. Not the Australian prodigy Cam Myers. Not the former Olympic silver medallist Timothy Cheruiyot.

This Commonwealth Games men's mile was his race, in his country, in front of his people. This gold medal really meant something.

Kerr's explosion of joy after he crossed the line and swaddled himself in a Saltire - having conducted the crowd during his final few strides - made that clear.

And so did his halting attempts to sing along with Flower of Scotland, the 28-year-old repeatedly stopping to bite his lip before wiping away tears from each eye.

"We rush through these moments so quickly," Kerr told BBC Sport Scotland, having spent the best part of 45 minutes doing selfies and signatures. "So I was just telling myself to slow down.

"In my head, I was flashing through all the hard moments and realising that I've come a long way. And to have Flower of Scotland playing versus the GB national anthem, it's just different. Not many times in my career I'll ever have that."

News.title: Teenager dies at Kendal Calling festival
News.content:
A teenage girl has died at the Kendal Calling festival in the early hours of the morning, police have said.

The 17-year-old suffered a medical episode at about 02:15 BST and was pronounced dead at the scene.

Cumbria Police said it was looking into the circumstances and wanted to speak to anyone who was in the area of the Calling Out tent and the Big Wheel around the time of the girl's death.

A spokesperson for the force said: "Officers are particularly keen to speak with a group of women who alerted first responders to the girl after becoming concerned for her welfare."

They said the girl's family had been informed and were being supported by specialist officers.

A Kendal Calling spokesperson said the festival team was supporting authorities with their investigation.

They said: "As soon as the individual became unwell, they were immediately attended to by our on-site security and medical teams.

"Paramedics and medical personnel provided emergency care at the scene and did everything they could to help."

The spokesperson added the team was "deeply saddened" by the teenager's death and extended "deepest sympathy" to her loved ones.

Follow BBC Cumbria on X, external, Facebook, external, Nextdoor and Instagram, external and listen to Radio Cumbria on BBC Sounds.

News.title: William and Kate bring children to second last day of Commonwealth Games
News.content:
The Prince and Princess of Wales have brought their three children to watch some of the final sporting events at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Cheering crowds at the city's OVO Hydro were treated to exhilarating performances in the netball semi-finals where the family watched New Zealand's 61-54 win over England.

Known as the Duke and Duchess of Rothesay while in Scotland, the couple also spent time meeting athletes, staff and volunteers during a slightly blustery visit to the venue on the River Clyde.

They then made their way to the Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome - where they chatted to British cyclist Dame Laura Kenny and sat one row behind another Olympic cycling champion, Sir Chris.

News.title: Mission to recover bodies continues after British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja and team killed in Pakistan avalanche

An operation to retrieve the bodies of an international climbing expedition continued on Pakistan’s Broad Peak on Sunday after it was confirmed that renowned Nepali-British mountaineer Nirmal Purja and nine others had been killed in an avalanche.

Purja was leading a 10-person expedition to summit Broad Peak, the world’s 12th tallest mountain located on the border with China, when the avalanche struck at midday on Thursday.

Statements on Saturday from Purja’s mountaineering company and the Nepali government confirmed that all members of the team had died, and on Sunday local officials said the bodies of five climbers had been retrieved so far.

Elite Exped said in a statement on social media: “Today it is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal 'Nimsdai' Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak.”

“We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive.”

open image in gallery Nirmal Purja is among those confirmed dead after his team was hit by an avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak ( Reuters )

Nepal prime minister Balendra Shah said the tragic loss of six Nepalese and four foreign climbers, including team members from the US, Oman, China and Pakistan, “has shocked us”.

"Only [the] physical journey of the climbers has stopped. But the history of their courage, dedication and contributions will always remain alive and inspiring," Mr Shah said.

Purja’s remains are among those yet to be recovered from the mountain, although all 10 bodies have been located. Recovery operations continue, involving both helicopters and ground teams.

American climber Sarah Mallory Geis was among the first victims of the avalanche identified on Friday, as drone footage showed signs of several more bodies in the search area that ground teams had been unable to reach due to bad weather.

On Sunday, Mingma David Sherpa, a Nepali mountaineer and expedition leader who is part of a ground recovery team, said they plan to move the bodies to Camp I and transfer them to another camp by Monday.

If conditions remain favourable, rescuers will then attempt to airlift the bodies by helicopter from the Japanese Camp, he said.

Sherpa said the operation's primary objective is to recover the climbers with dignity and return them to their families.

open image in gallery In this photo released by the Alpine Club of Pakistan on Friday, members of a mountaineer rescue team prepare to depart from an airbase on a search operation for climbers missing after an avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak ( AP )

Sajid Hussain, deputy director of the tourism department of Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan, said the rescue operation was ongoing.

"Rescue teams have successfully identified the location of the ‌victims; however, they have not yet been able to recover and bring them down safely," he told ​Reuters.

While drone surveillance and aerial reconnaissance had helped identify the exact location, reaching the dead and safely recovering ‌them remains a difficult task, he said.

The area ‌in which the operation is taking place is “remote and difficult”, said Sajid Hussain, deputy director of the tourism department in Gilgit-Baltistan.

Geis, 39, a resident of San Antonio, was an avid traveller who loved being outdoors, according to her Instagram page.

She announced on social media earlier this year that she was closing her pilates studio to take “a giant leap of faith into the unknown to see where life goes. I have a sneaking suspicion there will be lots of helmets, harnesses, and crampons involved”.

Tributes have poured in for all the climbers, with those who knew them expressing shock and sadness over the deaths.

The Prince of Wales expressed his profound sorrow, describing British citizen Purja as "one of the world’s greatest mountaineers" and "truly unique".

In a social media post on Saturday evening, Prince William shared his condolences. "I was truly saddened to hear of the tragic death of Nirmal Purja and those who lost their lives in the avalanche on Broad Peak," he wrote.

UK defence secretary Wes Streeting said in a post on X: "Incredibly sad to learn of the passing of Nirmal (Nims) Purja and those he was climbing with.

"He was an inspirational man who served in our Armed Forces for many years – and whose incredible mountaineering adventures are known the world over."

With an altitude of 8,051 metres (26,414 feet), Broad Peak is considered one of the most challenging mountains to climb in Pakistan. It saw its first successful ascent in 1957 when an Austrian expedition reached the summit.

The team of 10 was last in contact with their tour operator at 9am local time on Thursday. An avalanche struck the team when they were ascending from Camp II to Camp III at an approximate altitude of 6,600 metres, the commissioner of Gilgit-Baltistan announced late that night.

open image in gallery Members of a mountaineer rescue team pose for a photo with the honorary general secretary of Alpine Club of Pakistan, Ayaz Ahmed Shigri, centre, before departing from an airbase on a search operation for climbers missing after an avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak, in Skardu ( AP )

The rescue mission began at 8.30am on Friday after the tour agency made a formal request to the Pakistan army, which then deployed three helicopters to join the effort.

But later on Friday it was announced that rescue teams were stuck at base camp because of challenging weather conditions.

Purja was a British citizen who was awarded an MBE by the late Queen in 2018 for his achievements in extreme high-altitude mountaineering.

In 2019 he smashed the speed record for scaling the world’s 14 highest peaks, summiting them in just over six months compared to the prior record of around eight years.

Though his time was eclipsed four years later by Norwegian climber Kristin Harila, Purja’s efforts were immortalised in the popular Netflix documentary, 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible. It charted Purja's ambitious “Project Possible”, documenting his journey starting with Nepal’s Annapurna on 23 April 2019, through Everest in May and finishing after 189 days with K2 in July.

As summer temperatures soar, many gardeners face the annual dilemma of leaving their beloved plants vulnerable to scorching heat and drought during holiday periods.

However, with a warming climate, experts suggest a range of resilient species can flourish even in arid conditions. Julian Palphramand, head of plants at British Garden Centres, the UK’s largest family-owned garden centre group, highlights suitable options.

He advises: "Anything Mediterranean, from lavender to lamb’s ear (Stachys byzantine) through to cistus should be fine. Herbs such as rosemary and anything with slightly furry grey leaves tend to tolerate heat and drought quite well. Succulent types like sempervivums, echeverias, aloes or aeoniums are pretty resilient."

Here, he offers his top five drought-resistant plants.

1. Agapanthus

open image in gallery An agapanthus flower ( Alamy/PA )

The South African perennial, known as the African lily, produces large blue drumstick-headed flowers in summer, although there are also white and pink varieties.

“It has relatively fleshy leaves, loves heat and doesn’t like cold or wet, so the hotter the better, and the less moisture that’s in and around the top of the roots for any long periods is a good thing.

“Agapanthus like to be constricted in their root structure, so pots are perfect. If you’ve a real hot, sunny location on a patio or at the front of the house, agapanthus is a perfect one and the flowers last for ages.”

2. Achillea (yarrow)

“This is a classic perennial that adores full sun and well-drained soil, so not much water. It is drought-tolerant and the flowers just keep going. If you cut it back after flowering – do the Chelsea chop – you’ll probably get two, if not three, flowering repeats.”

Wild common yarrow is a spreading native wildflower with flat heads of small white, cream or pink flowers in summer, but breeding has introduced other colours including terracotta oranges and golds.

“There are varieties that are bred to be a bit more compact for pots, such as the Milly Rock series, and others that are a bit looser, taller, more middle-of-the-border traditional, like the standard Achillea millefolium.”

3. Sedum

open image in gallery Sedum 'Autumn Joy' ( Alamy/PA )

“Sedums to some people are a bit of a Marmite plant, a bit like euphorbias. People sometimes don’t like the fleshiness of them but I love them, and so do garden pollinators.

“They provide lots of much-needed pollen when a lot of other plants are going over through the late summer and autumn and there are many varieties to choose from.

“They will tolerate being in full sun with very little water. They remain upright. There are more rockery-type varieties and there are more upright ones like ‘Autumn Joy’, then you’ve the crawling, rambling varieties which stay close to the ground, the traditional stonecrop varieties.”

“Sedums won’t flower as prolifically if there isn’t much sun,” he continues. “The sunnier it is, the more flowers you’ll get and the longer the flowers will last.”

4. Eryngium (sea holly) and echinops (blue globe thistle)

These spiny, architectural perennials thrive in full sun with very well-draining, poor to moderately fertile soil which can be gravelly, sandy or chalky. They develop deep taproots providing drought tolerance and stability, forming clumps which get larger each year.

Both are blue types loved by bees throughout summer and are cottage garden perennials which thrive in full sun and are tolerant of drought.

5. Certain herbs

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

Lavender, rosemary, oregano and thyme love the sun and are a magnet for pollinating insects. You can easily grow them in pots, but, if you’re going away, move them to a semi-shaded area while you are away to give them a little protection.

“They won’t suffer from being in the sun, but they will suffer from a lack of water if you are away longer than a week,” Palphramand warns.

“You might even consider bringing them inside and treating them like a houseplant while you’re away because there’s not going to be any heating on and the house might not be as hot as the sunny location outside.”

Find a north-facing windowsill that’s bright without being in full sun to place your herbs while you’re on holiday.

France’s vast wildfire near Bordeaux, which scorched an area four times the size of Paris and forced 224,000 people to evacuate, remained contained Sunday but was still burning. Hundreds of kilometers (miles) away, a newer blaze in Provence had stopped advancing overnight but was not yet contained.

About 3,000 firefighters remained deployed across the two fronts, extinguishing hot spots, cutting firebreaks and securing areas of burned forest as high temperatures and wind threatened to breathe new life into smoldering embers.

The fire in the Gironde region burned about 420 square kilometers (162 square miles) in just 10 days before authorities declared its advance stopped over the weekend.

“The fire is now fixed, which does not mean that the fire is extinguished,” the Gironde prefecture said Sunday, using the French firefighting term for a blaze that has been contained within its perimeter.

The region remained under France’s highest red forest-fire alert. Dry conditions and soaring temperatures in Bordeaux, along with afternoon winds, risked rekindling flames.

Additional firefighters from Ukraine, Lithuania and French Polynesia were expected Sunday and Monday to reinforce the operation.

Human-caused climate change doubled the chances of extreme fire conditions for the flames in France, scientists at World Weather Attribution calculated in a rapid analysis Thursday, conducted while fires were still burning.

Europe is the world’s fastest-warming continent, with temperatures increasing at twice the speed as the global average since the 1980s, according to the European Union’s Copernicus Climate Change Service.

Blaze in Provence has stopped expanding but not yet contained

The Gironde blaze prompted one of the largest peacetime evacuations in modern French history. Many thousands of people remained displaced or unable to reach their homes.

In the southeastern Var department, meanwhile, nearly 1,500 firefighters were battling a separate fire that tore through roughly 18 square kilometers — seven square miles — in little more than a day.

Authorities said the blaze in the Gros Bessillon hills was stabilized Sunday morning, meaning its perimeter had not expanded overnight. But unlike the Gironde fire, it had not yet been declared contained.

Firefighting aircraft supported crews working to keep the flames away from villages set among the vineyards, olive groves and wooded hills of the region known as Green Provence.

About 2,500 people were evacuated as the fire threatened communities.

The blaze was the fourth major fire to strike the central Var since July 19. A separate, smaller fire near Brignoles earlier in the week forced Hollywood star George Clooney and his family, along with about 700 other residents, to evacuate before it was brought under control.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said France’s wildfires were generally under control but cautioned that conditions remained highly changeable.

Lecornu also announced the appointment of a national coordinator to oversee reconstruction in fire-ravaged areas. More than 1,170 square kilometers (452 square miles) have burned across France since the beginning of the year.

———

Adamson reported from Paris.

A centenarian has marked her 105th birthday in remarkable style by receiving 105 cards from across the globe.

Mary Davidson Smith, a resident at Care UK’s Murrayside care home in Edinburgh, expressed having a "wonderful time" reading the well-wishes, which arrived following an appeal by the home.

Cards travelled from as far afield as Singapore for her July celebration.

Ms Smith also holds the rare distinction of receiving a card from King Charles, having previously received one from the late Queen Elizabeth.

She celebrated her milestone with a "wonderful family day" and enjoyed afternoon tea with friends at Murrayside.

open image in gallery Ms Smith celebrated her milestone with a ‘wonderful family day’ and enjoyed afternoon tea with friends at Murrayside ( PA )

Born in Korea, Mary lived internationally during her youth, including periods in England, Canada, and the US.

She later joined the Royal Navy and met her future husband, British Army officer Charles Wynard Davidson Smith, while posted in Washington DC.

They went on to live in Edinburgh where they raised two sons, Neil and Mark, and Ms Smith now has four grandchildren.

Ms Smith has already made plans for her 106th birthday and hopes to celebrate with a “good strong whisky”, she said.

Remarking on her birthday cards, she said: “This is incredible! I’ve never seen so many cards, and they’re all for me.”

Her afternoon tea was prepared by the care home’s chef Jose.

Upon seeing her birthday meal, Ms Smith joked: “I’m glad you didn’t have 105 candles; I don’t have enough breath for that!”

Asked for her secret to a long and happy life, she said: “I enjoy it – keep on going.”

Ms Smith also said she came from a “long line of others that have lived long lives”.

The care home resident was recently reunited with a special Korean outfit she wore as a young girl almost 100 years ago.

open image in gallery Born in Korea, Mary lived internationally during her youth, including periods in England, Canada, and the US. ( PA )

During a special tour of the National Museum of Scotland officials took her on a private tour of the gallery and reunited her with the outfit.

Comprising a hat, bag and a wraparound jacket – known as a chimageogori – the outfit was described as a charming example of traditional Korean dress, or hanbok.

Suzanne Welsh, home manager at Murrayside care home, said: “It was a real joy to celebrate Mary’s 105th birthday.

“She is a much-loved resident who always has so many wonderful stories to share about her remarkable life.

“Mary is a huge part of the Murrayside family and is always keen to participate, whether it’s getting outdoors, church activities or quizzes.

“She also enjoys joining in with the singing sessions and meeting up with friends at coffee mornings.

“At Murrayside, we are committed to ensuring that residents continue to lead fulfilling and exciting lives.

“The team are super pleased to have reached our target of 105 cards – Mary was overjoyed to have received so much love and well wishes from people all over the world.

“Cheers to Mary!”

Vincent Pastore, best known for playing Salvatore “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero on The Sopranos, has died. He was 80.

The star was reportedly found dead Saturday in his Bronx, New York home by a neighbor after he had not been seen or heard from in the past three days.

An investigation has been launched into the circumstances of his death, Deadline reported.

The Independent has contacted the NYPD for comment.

In a statement to The Independent, his agent Bob McGowen said he only found out about Pastore’s death Saturday morning.

open image in gallery ‘Sopranos’ star Vincent Pastore (far right) was found dead in his Bronx home ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery Pastore was remembered as ‘a great guy’ who would help anyone ( Getty Images for Tribeca Festiva )

Remembering him as “such a great guy” who would help anyone, McGowen added: “I am just so sad of this passing. It’s hard to believe. I just spoke to him a couple days ago.”

Pastore was born July 14, 1946, in the Bronx to an Italian-American family. After graduating from New Rochelle High School in 1964, he enlisted in the U.S. Navy during the Vietnam War.

Following three years of service, Pastore studied drama at Pace University. He ultimately left after three years, due to difficulty finding acting jobs. He instead turned to the nightclub business, going on to own the now-defunct rock club and bar Crazy Horse in New Rochelle.

During a night out with actor brothers Matt and Kevin Dillon, who were regulars of Crazy Horse, The Pope of Greenwich Village was playing on the TV.

“Matty said, ‘You could do the work that these guys are doing,’ pointing to [future Sopranos co-star] Frank Vincent and Tony Musante,” Pastore previously remembered, according to The Hollywood Reporter.

open image in gallery Pastore starred as a main member in the first two seasons of 'The Sopranos,' later making brief appearances in later seasons ( Getty )

He eventually made his professional acting debut in Nancy Savoca’s True Love (1989), starring Annabella Sciorra and Ron Eldard. It was his performance in the romcom that led casting director Ellen Lewis to hire him for a small, uncredited part in Martin Scorsese’s classic Goodfellas.

That same year, he also appeared in Penny Marshall’s Robin Williams and Robert De Niro-led melodrama Awakenings.

Pastore made a successful career out of playing gangsters in TV and movies. He starred in the 1996 biographical drama Gotti, about infamous mob boss John Gotti, alongside future Sopranos co-stars Tony Sirico, Frank Vincent and Dominic Chianese.

In 1999, he landed his breakout role as Salvatore “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero in the six-season Emmy-winning HBO crime drama, The Sopranos. He starred as a series regular on the first two seasons before his character was killed off at the end of season two. He returned for occasional appearances in flashbacks and dream sequences in later seasons.

His other notable acting credits included The Jerky Boys: The Movie (1995), DreamWorks’ Shark Tale (2004) and Revolver (2005). His last role was voicing a talking llama in 2025 episode of the horror series Yellowjackets.

Pastore is survived by his daughter, Renee.

News.title: Watch: People flee In-N-Out after gunman carrying long rifle opens fire
News.content:
People fled and ran for cover after a shooting incident at the In-N-Out in Twin Falls, Idaho.

At least three people were killed and seven others were injured in a mass shooting on Saturday (1 August), according to police and local officials.

Video taken by a driver from across the street captured the suspected gunman, who appeared to be dressed in black, approaching a white car carrying a long rifle. He then opened the driver-side door and popped the trunk as the terrified people nearby ran from the restaurant for safety.

The suspected shooter, an unidentified male, is dead, Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said at a press conference. He described the scene as “tragic” and “chaotic.”

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Kerr wins by a mile: Scot claims Commonwealth gold to emulate Bannister
News.content:
For many the 100m is the Blue Riband event the one everyone wants to watch and the race that steals all the headlines. For these Commonwealth Games, however, tonight’s mile race is the one that has grabbed all the attention – and it is not hard to see why.

Josh Kerr, fresh from his new world record of 3:42.66 (a time that beat a mark that had stood since 1999) takes on fellow Scot Jake Wightman and Australia’s new superstar Cameron Myers. Three great runners over a distance that evokes sepia-tinted memories of Roger Bannister and the seminal four-minute mark.

Some of you may be wondering why the mile is back at an international event. Well, Seb Coe, the president of World Athletics and someone who broke the mile record three times, says the race distance is easy to understand and resonates with fans. And, coming on the back of Kerr’s world record, who can argue with him?

This is the first time the mile has been run at the games since 1966 and the hope is that tonight’s final matches the Miracle Mile run in 1954. Earlier that year Bannister broke the four-minute barrier, only for Australia’s John Landy to go lower with a time of 3:58.0 soon after. The Games in Vancouver were the first time two sub-four minuters had gone head-to-head. And the race didn’t disappoint – Bannister beating Landy with a time of 3:58.8 minutes. The Australian also ran under four minutes, making it the first time two men had done so in the same race.

Obviously all three of the expected main protagonists will go well under four minutes, but if they can recreate the drama of the 1954 final then we’ll have a race to savour.

Stay here for all the action with the gun set to go off at 8.55.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

Sports.title: Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear
Sports.content:
Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear

Manchester United have already been busy in the transfer market under Michael Carrick and some exits could be on the cards before the end of the window but one deal is already under threat

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has some decisions to make in the transfer market (Image: Getty Images)

Joshua Zirkzee might just have seen his Manchester United exit route blocked, with Juventus pursuing alternative targets. The Dutchman was expected to leave Old Trafford this summer following a disappointing couple of seasons.

‌



Zirkzee, 25, joined the club from Bologna for a fee of £36.5m in 2024 but he has gone on to score just nine goals since then - just five of those coming in the Premier League. It was previously suggested that United were happy to cut their losses on him this summer.

‌



A return to Serie A was touted for the former Bayern Munich man, with Juventus emerging as potential suitors. But a switch to Turin now looks unlikely given Juventus’ own business.

‌



According to reports in Italy, the Old Lady are closing in on a permanent deal for French striker Randal Kolo Muani for a fee of around £42m (€50m), while they have also completed a move for Bayer Leverkusen’s Kerim Alajbegovic.

Amad and Leny Yoro in total agreement after JJ Gabriel makes Man Utd debut READ MORE :

Given those two moves, it appears unlikely that Juventus will want to sign Zirkzee as well. The only route to a move to Turin appears to be a swap deal involving the Dutch forward and Francisco Conceição, albeit it remains to be seen whether that is an avenue that the Red Devils want to explore.

He does also appear to have other interest, specifically from Ajax and Premier League sides, but whether that becomes a tangible move, is another matter. It could leave Zirkzee in a very tricky spot, with Carrick appearing to signal that the forward has little future at Old Trafford, having only given him a brief cameo in the pre-season win against Atletico Madrid.

‌



Fellow forward Bryan Mbeumo instead started centrally and enjoyed a productive evening by scoring twice. Speaking about his role, the Cameroonian said: “Obviously, I’m lucky to be able to play a different position and I try to give my best. It depends on the games (where I play).

View 2 Images Zirkzee was only handed a brief cameo vs Atletico Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

“We try to get ready for the first game of the season and we work really hard on the training so it’s really important to have good results as well.

Article continues below

He added: “Obviously I’m always really challenging myself every time and will never regret having this challenge.”

Away from Zirkzee and Mbeumo, United could potentially be left with a decision to make over Benjamin Sesko. According to reports in Germany, Bayern Munich remain interested in the former RB Leipzig man, albeit their focus for now remains on agreeing a new deal with star forward Harry Kane.

Sports.title: Arsenal forced to release short statement after Christos Tzolis debut
Sports.content:
Arsenal forced to release short statement after Christos Tzolis debut

Arsenal signing Christos Tzolis made his official debut for the Gunners in a pre-season friendly against Girona, during which the club were forced to issue a short statement

View 2 Images Arsenal were forced to release a statement during Christos Tzolis' debut (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal were forced to release a short statement after supporters were left frustrated by streaming issues during Christos Tzolis' debut against Girona.

‌



The Gunners continued their unbeaten start to pre-season with a comfortable 4-1 victory over the Spanish side on Saturday, but some fans missed parts of the action after experiencing technical problems while trying to watch the game.

‌



Arsenal had made the friendly available via Arsenal.com and the club's official app, but issues with both platforms meant some fans were unable to access the stream. The club later moved coverage to YouTube, where the match was made available for free.

‌



"Arsenal supporters, apologies for the inconvenience. We're working through some issues on Arsenal.com and The Arsenal App," the club said in a statement posted on social media. "Tonight's game is now being streamed for free on our YouTube channel."

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mikel Arteta directly pressed on Vinicius Jr before ending Arsenal press conference suddenly READ MORE :

The match also marked the first official appearance of summer signing Christos Tzolis, who wasted little time making an impression after joining from Club Brugge in a £34million deal last month.

‌



The Greece international opened his Arsenal account by doubling their advantage on the half-hour mark after Kai Havertz had put Mikel Arteta's side ahead in the 16th minute. Arnau Martinez pulled one back shortly after half-time, but Max Dowman restored Arsenal's two-goal cushion minutes later before Gabriel Jesus added another to complete a convincing win.

The fixture was Arsenal's second of five pre-season matches this summer, following last week's 3-0 victory over MK Dons in a behind-closed-doors friendly, where Tzolis also impressed.

View 2 Images Christos Tzolis (R) scored Arsenal's second goal in a 4-1 win over Girona (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Arteta's side will now face Real Betis on Wednesday before taking on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup next Sunday. They will then conclude their 2026/27 preparations against Como - managed by former Arsenal star Cesc Fabregas - four days before their Community Shield clash with Manchester City.

While Tzolis remains Arsenal's only major arrival of the summer so far, the Gunners continue to work on further reinforcements. They are reportedly closing in on a deal for Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes, with the Brazilian said to be edging closer to a move after the two clubs made progress over a fee believed to be around £80million.

Arsenal have also been linked with a sensational move for Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr, who is currently locked in talks over a new contract at the Bernabeu. The winger has entered the final year of his deal, putting pressure on Madrid to resolve his future, although any potential transfer would likely require a fee well in excess of £100m.

Article continues below

In terms of departures, Arsenal have reportedly agreed to sell Christian Norgaard to Everton for £7m. The move would take their summer sales beyond £40m following the departures of Leandro Trossard, Jakub Kiwior and Karl Hein.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed

Gianni Infantino has come under waves of criticism for a controversial World Cup as well as FIFA plans to sell commercial stakes in their premier footballing competitions

View Image Gianni Infantino has been criticised this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino looked to bag a staggering £22.2million salary through FIFA's proposed Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, only for the proposal to spark widespread fury. UEFA and the FA condemned plans for the organisation to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, with member associations vowing to boycott the tournament altogether.

‌



As per the Times, Infantino could have made tens of millions of pounds through the scheme, which has since been canned following backlash. Meanwhile, UEFA claim that they have lost confidence in the FIFA president as a result.

‌



A statement from the European football governing body read: "We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

‌



Gianni Infantino is so delusional he does not know his time is well and truly up READ MORE :

“It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental.

"No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence, but also that of many other members of the football family."

The English FA also supported UEFA's stance, with a spokesperson for the organisation adding: " We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart."

‌



CONCACAF, meanwhile, are in favour of a " comprehensive reckoning" of Infantino's presidency, adding in their own statement: " It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first. This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour."

That would have seen him land a salary of around £22.2m annually, before bonuses. FIFA refute claims that the idea was discussed, however.

A statement from Infantino read: " The FFE project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA member associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

"And, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the member associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA council, the confederations and wider stakeholders.

Sports.content:
Arsenal put FIVE title-winners up for sale as Man Utd ‘investigate’ transfer deal

Both Manchester United and Arsenal have been active in the transfer market this summer and the two Premier League rivals could potentially do business together before the end of the window

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is keen on more business this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United are mulling over a move for Myles Lewis-Skelly, with Arsenal open to offers for a number of stars. The Red Devils are keen to add to their fullback options before next month’s deadline.

‌



Newcastle’s Lewis Hall has emerged as a prime target for Michael Carrick but a deal could be difficult. The Magpies have already lost Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer, while Bruno Guimaraes appears to be on the verge of a move to Arsenal.

‌



That might make a move for Hall considerably more expensive, which has forced United to look at potential alternatives. According to The Independent, Arsenal academy graduate Lewis-Skelly is one of the options being considered.

‌



It is being reported that the Red Devils have a long-standing interest in the 19-year-old and are investigating whether a deal is possible this summer. There was a ‘possibility’ of a move last term, with the defender out of favour but he managed to re-establish himself in the first team towards the end of the campaign.

Mikel Arteta directly pressed on Vinicius Jr before ending Arsenal press conference suddenly READ MORE :

As it stands, Lewis-Skelly is one that Arsenal would want to keep but that situation could change should they complete mega-money deals for Vinicius Jr and Guimaraes.

There are however a number of other players that the North London side would prefer to let go in an attempt to balance the books. It is suggested that Arsenal will listen to offers for Reiss Nelson, Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli and Viktor Gyokeres, while midfielder Christian Norgaard looks set for a move to Everton.

‌



On Arsenal’s business for the next month, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said: “Well, we are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear. We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else.

View 2 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly is of interest to Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

“And you can just see it. The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing, we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do.”

Article continues below

He added: “Because the margins are very small. And because we want to get better and the level is going to increase, we need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don't have in the team, to have bigger margins. And that's the way we have to think.”

Arsenal have already made three signings this summer, with Christos Tzolis and Ilian Meslier having arrived, while Piero Hincapie has been signed permanently. When it comes to the Red Devils, they have also completed three deals for Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's ill-fated scheming does not mean a 64-team World Cup should be written off
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's ill-fated scheming does not mean a 64-team World Cup should be written off

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is somehow still clinging to his job but a consultation process is still taking place over the possible expansion of the World Cup in 2030

View 4 Images Cape Verde and their goalkeeper Vozinha captured the imagination of football fans around the world (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The news - the predictable news - that FIFA has already begun a consultation process ahead of making a decision about expanding the World Cup to include 64 teams was met not only with widespread incredulity but with utter cynicism.

‌



And there was one of the many fundamental problems with Gianni Infantino’s heinous, thankfully ill-fated scheme to sell off a chunk of the World Cup to billionaire cronies.

‌



It meant everything suggested by FIFA will feel rotten. This expansion idea was immediately seen, certainly in Europe, as just another ruse to make more money for FIFA and for the private investors that Infantino wanted to ingratiate himself with - and make fortunes from. No-one could have been blamed for looking at it from that point of view.

‌



UEFA declare loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino in bombshell new statement READ MORE :

The secret of comedy is timing, but there was nothing funny about FIFA saying they are, essentially, rushing through their consultation period - a decision will be made as soon as August 14 - just a couple of days after Infantino’s plot to raise $20billion by auctioning off rights packages to the World Cup was revealed. Bigger World Cup, more money for those private investor mates that, mercifully, will now not be directly involved in the tournament.

No wonder the news that the prospect of a 64-team World Cup is being accelerated by FIFA fat-cats was met with almost complete scorn. That is where power-crazed, money-obsessed Infantino has taken FIFA.

Yet would a 64-team World Cup be that bad? If the extra revenue was not going to private investors - and that prospect has been summarily headed off by UEFA’s threat of a boycott - would a 64-team World Cup be one of FIFA’s worst offences? No.

‌



View 4 Images Curacao were another small nation to make their mark on World Cup 2026 (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Hands up, I was against the tournament being expanded to 48 from 32 teams but was soon converted once Cape Verde started doing their stuff. I was converted when Curacao equalised against Germany, even though they were hammered 7-1.

I was converted by the entertainment provided by the group stages. I was converted by the joy of every nation’s set of fans.

‌



The only downside I could find was that the third games in the group stages were open to contrivance. That is because whittling 48 teams down to 32 for the knockout stages involves having eight third-placed finishers as qualifiers.

As it happened, there was no evidence of contrivance, but quite simply, 64 into 32 goes better. Sixteen groups of four, top two in each group qualify. Easy.

View 4 Images Gianni Infantino is under increasing pressure to stand down as FIFA president (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



The next World Cup in 2030 - the centenary edition - is being staged in Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay hosting opening-round matches. There will be enough venues to accommodate 64 teams.

As UEFA and its president Aleksander Ceferin are now at permanent odds with FIFA and Infantino, they might not like the idea of an expansion to 64 teams. They will probably oppose it.

Yet the Euros is a 24-team competition, meaning 43.63 per cent of its member nations qualify for the finals. A 64-team World Cup would mean 30.34 per cent of FIFA member nations would qualify.

‌



View 4 Images Spain lifted the World Cup trophy at the end of a 48-team tournament that was widely deemed a success (Image: David Ramos/Getty Images)

Those of us who were originally in the camp that thought the World Cup should be for the elite only have long lost the argument. It turns out it was not a bad one to lose. Did you begrudge any of the teams at the 2026 World Cup their time in the sun?

And now it is a 48-team tournament - there will be no consultation process about any possible reduction in competitors - what is an extra 16 teams between friends? Italy might even qualify.

Article continues below

Understandably, an expansion would be negatively linked with Infantino’s scheming. But he will be long gone by then, surely. And the 64 teams who compete at the 2030 World Cup can enjoy themselves, untainted by his presidency and private ownership.
