'I watch myself for analytical reasons,' White recently claimed to The Overlap. 'I watch England, maybe, but I'm always busy doing something. I wouldn't just sit down and watch a game.

'I didn't ever watch football when I was younger. I still don't now.'

But, as is the case with Van Gerwen, it's not all hate with White. He just wants to be out there playing.

'I just loved the game,' he continued. 'I was always playing it, never watching.

'So I don't know too much about the older generations, but I know (Patrick) Vieira was a very good player. But I don't know the details.'

Ben White (right) has become known for his dislike of watching football

Serena Williams – Tennis

Serena Williams is perhaps the most famous name in women's tennis history, and one of the most dominant too.

'I don't love tennis today, but I'm here, and I can't live without it,' she told TennisNow in 2012. 'So I'm still here and I don't want to go anywhere any time soon.'

That's despite winning seven Australian Opens, seven Wimbledon titles, six US Opens and three French Opens. But it's not just tennis – it's sport on the whole.

'It's not that I've fallen out of love, I've actually never liked sports, and I never understood how I became an athlete,' she continued. 'I don't like working out, I don't like anything that has to do with working physically.'

Not too much of an issue, though, it seems...

Serena Williams revealed in 2012 that she doesn't love tennis - or sport on the whole

Nick Kyrgios – Tennis

Tennis bad boy Nick Kyrgios has had a bit of a love-hate relationship with his sport.

The Australian, who is planning retirement at the age of 31, reached his first Grand Slam final in 2022 at Wimbledon. He would lose to Novak Djokovic, but has also regularly made headlines for his actions away from the actual tennis, such as his shouting during matches.

One wonders if his relationship with tennis is related to that. He said in 2015: 'I don't really like the sport of tennis that much. I don't love it.'

He does, though, have love for a different sport.

'It was crazy when I was 14,' he continued. 'I was all for basketball and I made the decision to play tennis. I got pushed by my parents and to this day I can still say I don't love the sport. It is just crazy how things go.

'It's good when you're out there on a tennis court. There's nowhere to hide. It's all you, tactically, physically, mentally. But I just love basketball, I love the sport. I always have. I try when I'm on the road with tennis not to watch too many basketball videos and stuff like that, to keep me focused, but it's tough.'

What could have been.

Nick Kygrios has a love-hate relationship with the sport - and would rather have been a basketball player

Mark Williams – Snooker

Things seem to be going a little better for Mark Williams since his comments in 2019, when he became one of the few athletes to actively say they 'hate' their sport.

Currently World No 8 and a 2025 World Championship finalist, the Welshman was going through a tough patch back in 2019 when he had just beaten Fraser Patrick 6-2 in the first round of the UK Snooker Championship.

Despite actually being ranked No 3 in the world, Williams had failed to win a ranking event all year. He lashed out at snooker, and, like Kyrgios, his mind was elsewhere.

'I really struggled but somehow he struggled more than me and made it easy for me on a couple of frames,' Williams said. 'It's going all right, I'm enjoying myself when I'm on the golf course.'

When questioned on snooker, he added: 'Hate it. I'm just enjoying playing golf more.'

He had also talked about retirement in 2017, before going on to become world champion for a third time a year later.

Maybe he feels differently now.

Mark Williams admitted to 'hating' snooker in 2019 after teasing retirement a few years earlier

Tyson Fury – Boxing

Potentially the biggest name in modern boxing doesn't actually like boxing.

Tyson Fury has retired and un-retired countless times, but attributes his many returns to an addiction that helps him deal with his mental health struggles.

'I've tried to walk away many times and been unsuccessful,' he told DAZN in 2024. 'I meant it when I retired after Dillian Whyte back in 2022, I really meant that wholeheartedly. I could have put my hand on the Bible and meant it, but it was difficult to let it go.

'I've been in love with boxing from a little boy. It's been a love-hate relationship. When it's good, it's very good and when it's bad, it's very toxic. Now I am a fully grown adult with a family of my own.

'I wanted to walk away a lot of times but it always drags me back. Boxing is an addiction. It abuses my body, my mind, my soul. But I feel like it takes me to ecstasy. The rush is unbelievable. It gives me the biggest highs ever, but it also gives me the lowest lows. Boxing is more addictive than any drug ever. Ever. You can't let it go.'

It only takes a quick viewing of his reality show to see how much his family have begged him to pack it in. It seems, though, their words aren't enough.

Fury is set to take on Anthony Joshua in an all-British mega-fight later this year, having eased past Mariusz Wach last weekend. After that, he may well retire again – but will seemingly always keep on coming back.

Tyson Fury has tried to retire from boxing a number of times but finds himself returning

Benoit Assou-Ekotto – Football

A pattern emerges in the list of players who don't like their sport. They engage with it in some form all the time – every decision is based on their career, they have to analyse everything about it, and they spend most of their time performing it.

'I play it enough, don't I?' former Tottenham full back Benoit Assou-Ekotto once argued in an interview with Sky Sports.

'I don't watch football. I don't talk about football away from the game either. I suppose that is unusual. My interests are my friends and music, especially hip-hop. I like Ice Cube and 50 Cent.'

Assou-Ekotto played more than 200 times for Spurs, and didn't do too much wrong. Perhaps his argument proves you don't have to be totally obsessed with what you are doing to reach the top level – or maybe it suggests he could have gone higher if he was.

Former Tottenham defender Benoit Assou-Ekotto (right) is another sports star who does not enjoy watching their sport

Andre Agassi wrote in his autobiography that he 'hates' tennis despite his widespread success

Andre Agassi – Tennis

We have saved the most brutal for last – eight-time Grand Slam tennis champion Andre Agassi hates tennis.

'I play tennis for a living even though I hate tennis,' he wrote in his autobiography. 'I hate it with a dark and secret passion and always have.'

Tell us what you really think, Andre.

It's unclear exactly why the American feels that way, but it could be something to do with top players being on tour for more than 30 weeks a year, having tennis dominate their lives, and the stress involved.

Agassi won all there was to win. Others on this list have too. Still – it is not always enough. Showing that, sometimes, being a sports star may not be all it can seem to be.

Sports.title: Inside the chaotic four days that have left Gianni Infantino fighting to stay in power, how arrogant FIFA president's gamble spectacularly backfired and the contenders looking to overthrow him after World Cup own goal
Sports.content:
It's only two weeks since Gianni Infantino joined President Donald Trump in handing over the Jules Rimet trophy to Spain in New Jersey, wearing a dark suit, blindingly white trainers and the self-satisfied grin of a man celebrating a World Cup triumph of his own.

The FIFA president declared the tournament - and its new 48-team format - a huge success after spending the previous six weeks flitting around North America in a private jet to see his vision become reality.

Anybody else might have been inclined to spend some time reflecting on a World Cup that produced more than its fair share of talking points, or even have some time off.

Not Infantino. He was already moving onto his next project; one that backfired spectacularly this week and has left the 56-year-old Swiss fighting to stay in power.

It took less than four days for his grand plan to sell off football’s crown jewel to private investors for £3.1billion to go up in smoke, from the bombshell news breaking at lunchtime on Tuesday to Infantino’s humiliating statement in the early hours of Saturday confirming it has been scrapped in the face of widespread opposition.

At the end of a seismic week for world football, it is hard to see how he can survive after leading confederations and even senior executives at FIFA turned on the embattled president, and UEFA made the first move towards removing him from office with a vote of no confidence on Saturday morning.

Just days after lauding the 2026 World Cup as a huge, almost personal, success Gianni Infantino saw his iron grip on FIFA's presidency unravel

Why did it unravel so quickly? How did Infantino, a skilled political figure, get it so horribly wrong?

It was clear this wasn’t going to end well from the immediate sense of shock and outrage when The Times revealed that Infantino wanted to create a subsidiary company called FIFA Forward Enterprise to run its flagship events, primarily the World Cup, in a deal that could be worth up to £15bn.

Private investors would have been able to buy stakes in FFE through a group led by Thrive Eternal, a US venture capital company founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared.

The 211 member associations were offered a £30m cut if they agreed with the proposals by September 19.

UEFA were the first to voice their opposition with a strongly worded statement agreed unanimously and co-signed by the English FA and Europe’s other 54 associations. They criticised Infantino for ‘a profound failure of leadership’ and presiding over ‘governance by intimidation’, adding: ‘None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.’

UEFA followed that up with a threat to boycott the World Cup if Infantino refused to back down and abandon his plans.

Two other Confederations then came out against Infantino on Thursday and Friday. CONCACAF, which represents 41 countries across North America, Central America and the Caribbean, rejected the proposal and expressed ‘deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal and the artificially short deadline imposed’.

The Asian Football Confederation followed, saying: ‘Football should never have been placed in such a position. It has exposed fundamental weaknesses in FIFA’s consultation and decision-making processes that must now be addressed.’

Infantino needed a majority of the 211 member nations to vote through his proposals, but already 136 of them were opposed to him.

He doubled down on Friday morning when FIFA issued a statement insisting that ‘nobody is selling football’ - but opposition was growing at an alarming rate.

New Prime Minister Andy Burnham weighed into the controversy, questioning whether Infantino is the right man to lead FIFA anymore.

‘This was an outrageous suggestion,’ said Burnham. ‘The idea that it could even be brought forward, in my view, shows that the FIFA president is the wrong man to lead the organisation.’

More damagingly for Infantino, two of his senior aides turned against him in the space of a few hours.

President of the US Soccer Federation Carlos Cordeiro was a key Infantino ally before he fell on his sword

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani has emerged as an early contender to stand against Infantino in March

Carlos Cordeiro, who was FIFA’s representative on the White House taskforce for the World Cup and at Infantino’s side throughout, said: ‘As a senior adviser to the FIFA president, a former banker, and a lifelong football fan, I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup.

‘I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for FIFA’s member associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.

‘Selling a permanent stake in football’s most valuable asset to raise $4.2bn makes little sense. It is mortgaging football’s future without any compelling justification.’

If that wasn’t bad enough for Infantino, FIFA’s chief operating officer Kevin Lamour then quit, claiming that Infantino had ‘deceived’ his own administration and accusing him of a ‘lie by omission’. He blasted the plans as a ‘the project of one person’.

‘This (lie) and unilateral exercise of power are not trivial,’ added Lamour. ‘They are indicative of a lack of trust, a lack of transparency, a lack of discernment, a lack of good governance. And a serious lack of respect.

‘Not only must this project not go ahead, but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.

‘My colleagues - some of whom have dedicated their lives to football - deserve better than contempt and intimidation.

‘The ball is now in the court of those who have the power to change things. I know I have a duty of loyalty to my employer. But I also, and above all, have a duty of loyalty to certain values and to the upbringing I have received, and a duty to support my colleagues. And if that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.’

Shortly after midnight, Infantino inevitably bowed to the pressure and announced he was scrapping the proposals because ‘it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place’.

If he thought that would be the end of the matter, however, it quickly became clear on Saturday that the implications could be far greater when UEFA declared a vote of no confidence in him.

Europe’s governing body hit out at Infantino for the ‘shabby, back-room, opaque deal he hatched’ and promised to work with the other confederations in world football to ‘identify those responsible and hold them to account’.

It added: ‘This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun.’

So what next for Infantino? He has been in power for 10 years and was expected to win re-election for a fourth term unopposed at the next FIFA congress in Morocco in March.

But with support dwindling fast and UEFA on the warpath, it looks increasingly likely that a rival candidate will stand against him.

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani has emerged as an early contender, along with current FIFA general secretary Mattias Granstrom and Dariusz Mioduski, a vice-president of the European Football Clubs body.

Two weeks after he had the whole world in his hands, it feels as though Gianni Infantino’s time is almost up.

Sports.title: The tactical shift that proves Enzo Maresca will not be a Pep Guardiola copycat, how new Man City boss may have discovered Antoine Semenyo's best position and the academy star ready to step up after dazzling display against Inter Milan
Sports.content:
The Enzo Maresca era at Manchester City is officially underway after his side lost 3-1 on penalties to lose the Asahi Super Dry Trophy to Inter Milan.

Inside the 50,000-seat Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong, Divin Mubama scored the first goal of the Maresca era after brilliant wing play by Antoine Semenyo, only for Inter Milan to respond through Benjamin Pavard.

While City were the better side in the second half, striking the post through youngster Ryan McAidoo, it ultimately went to penalties and despite a delightful Panenka penalty from Claudio Echeverri, misses from Rayan Ait-Nouri, Abdukodir Khusanov and Nico Gonzalez meant City came out as the runners-up.

Many of their World Cup stars are still to come back in and so this was a mixed-up group for Maresca to cut his teeth with.

Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the key things we learned from Maresca's first game in charge in Hong Kong.

The Enzo Maresca era at Manchester City is officially underway after facing Inter Milan in Asia

THE FODEN PUZZLE

There is so much for Enzo Maresca to get stuck into this pre-season but finding a formula to get the best out of Phil Foden should be top of the pile.

Foden has had seven weeks off to refresh, both physically and mentally, after a tough season where criticism was sharp and top performances felt few and far between, given what had come before.

Here was Foden wearing the captain's armband, playing as the No 10 in a side that had been built around him.

Maresca knows exactly what Foden can do, one of the Premier League's absolute best players when he's at the peak of his powers, and finding a way to consistently maximise that could be the difference between winning and losing the biggest prizes.

'He's very important, like the rest,' Maresca said in the lead-up. 'Knowing Phil from years ago, I know how good he is so it's my duty to try to help him to be the Phil that we all want.

'First of all, to be happy, to play football, for him is the most important thing. And as I said, Phil in a good condition and mood can help us to win games and titles - and that's what we want…'

First half here it felt like the game was passing Foden by; a couple of erroneous losses of possession and limited opportunities to build attacks were the headlines.

Second half, with Semenyo operating through the middle ahead of him, Foden looked sharper but still shy of the levels many are urging him to get back to.

Just under 70 minutes of action here for Foden was a reminder that while he is eager to be given a fresh start - and Maresca is ready to give him one - much more will be expected. Both player and manager need to find the formula for success.

Phil Foden showed flashes of what he can do but he needs to deliver much more this season

SHAPE WORK

This is one of the more interesting aspects of any opening pre-season game, particularly when a team is entering a new era following unprecedented success under its greatest ever manager.

So, no, this wasn't copy-and-paste of the Pep Guardiola era by Maresca.

What we saw instead was an aggressive 4-2-4 high press out of possession, with Foden pushed up high alongside striker Divin Mubama, while it was a 3-4-2-1 with the ball with Josko Gvardiol anchoring a back three.

It was not flawless, mind you, with any cheap turnovers of possession allowing Inter Milan to counter quickly, exploiting the space out wide with City's full-backs advanced up the pitch.

In the first half City's midfield was overcrowded and too much space was being afforded out wide. Tijjani Reijnders in particular struggled to influence the game alongside Mateo Kovacic.

There were times too when Maresca was barking at his players to press zonally, albeit the hope will be intensity can add into this when fitness builds up and more first team players add back in.

Inter Milan had chances and many were presented to them by City which will be cause for concern, particularly with space in the forward areas.

But City will be one of pre-season's most interesting watches to see how Maresca's methodology beds in in Manchester.

LEFT IS BEST FOR ANTOINE

When the teamsheet dropped to show Antoine Semenyo as the left winger, rather than the right, where Pep Guardiola liked to play him, there was a collective rejoicing in the City fanbase.

Semenyo is incredibly versatile and while he started out on the right in the early days at Bournemouth, he really kicked into gear as one of the Premier League's best players off the left for the Cherries.

And here in Hong Kong was a great deal of evidence as to why the left side is the best side for the Ghanaian.

One of the criticisms of Semenyo on the right is that there is a predictability to his movements in the final third.

Here against Inter Milan it was wholly unpredictable and therefore a nightmare assignment for Inter Milan's defenders, as Semenyo toyed with them, turning inside and out.

It was Semenyo's burst, really noticeable in the first half before he was moved centrally in the second, that teed up the first goal of the Maresca era when he glided past Andy Diouf and rolled it across for Divin Mubama to slot in.

Jeremy Doku will come back in to the fold but on this evidence, relocating Semenyo should not be top of Maresca's to-do list.

Antoine Semenyo was immense off the left, but saw his game shackled when moved inside

Ryan McAidoo turned Inter Milan's players inside-out in a really promising second half cameo

RYAN IS READY

For those who watch academy football regularly, the sight of Ryan McAidoo turning full-backs inside-out is one that you see on a weekly basis.

The question has been whether it will translate to the senior level. On this evidence, the answer is absolutely yes.

The 18-year-old's cameo in Hong Kong was bursting with quality as he had Inter Milan players bouncing off him, so strong is his low centre of gravity, and he even struck the post after a brilliant solo run.

One of the criticisms of City's wide players at times during the Guardiola era was that they appeared over-coached and had flair in their game limited in favour of ball security.

Well, McAidoo was a breath of fresh air here, running directly at players, relishing any and all one-versus-one match-ups and a bag of tricks that would have made Foden and Semenyo proud.

'He played as well as Semenyo for me,' former City winger Shaun Wright-Phillips said. 'He did more than impress... I loved it.'

Maresca can't help but have been impressed, too. McAidoo is ready.

Sports.title: Why Rob Key picked Stephen Fleming over England's up-and-coming coaches: The coaching 'shift' that has swept cricket, why foreigners are judged through a different prism and the county coach who has been harshly overlooked
Sports.content:
Why Rob Key picked Stephen Fleming over England's up-and-coming coaches: The coaching 'shift' that has swept cricket, why foreigners are judged through a different prism and the county coach who has been harshly overlooked

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

There are many reasons that few Englishmen go on to coach England these days: the results of those that have gone before hang heavy, a mistrust of the country’s embedded coaching system has developed and so has an infatuation with star names.

This century only Peter Moores (twice) and Chris Silverwood have been given the privilege of calling themselves Test coach and between them they lost more matches than they won - the numbers being 24 and 23 respectively.

That might appear to be a tough yardstick to be judged by, but such statistics will have influenced Rob Key in his decision to appoint New Zealander Stephen Fleming despite a lack of first-class coaching experience, ahead of Richard Dawson, perhaps the brightest coaching talent in the country and one with silverware on his CV.

Some will argue, perhaps with justification that Dawson’s achievements with two unfashionable counties have not been given commensurate weighting in this selection process. Gloucestershire supporters look back on their Lord’s one-day cup final win in 2015 as one of the club’s finest achievements while he has Glamorgan as high as fourth in the County Championship after his first season in charge concluded with promotion last September.

In between those two jobs, there was the small matter of overseeing an eight-match England Lions tour of Australia in early 2020, returning home undefeated having won the four-day ‘Test’ against Australia A.

On Friday, Key spoke of ‘working on’ homegrown coaches to ‘upskill’ them, saying more experiences needed to be created for them overseas. That such development would not be a quick fix. Yet Dawson’s very positive experience of winning in Australia was six years ago. He has knowledge of lots of conditions around the world garnered from various England tours.

With the appointment of Stephen Fleming, there is the suggestion that England have overlooked attracting one of their own - such as Richard Dawson

Fleming (left, with ex-team-mate and former England coach Brendon McCullum in 2008) is a much starrier name

It feels like a case of disregard for the coaching path from which Dawson - whose standoffish demeanour should not detract from the fact he is an excellent coach well respected by the country’s leading players - has emerged.

Key has shown little regard for the traditional level four coaching qualification that the ECB has asked the country’s best coaches to complete for the past quarter of a century, instead appointing those with limited or no coaching backgrounds in the form of former playing greats Brendon McCullum and Andrew Flintoff to high position.

Investment has been in inspiration not perspiration. Overall, McCullum has proved to be a success across four years and three England teams, but said early on: ‘Don’t expect me to be on the tools.’ But Flintoff has proved more of a mentor than coach since taking over the Lions two years ago, and will skip some of next winter’s programme in South Africa to coach Sydney Thunder in the Big Bash League.

It is part of a wider culture of ‘image’ taking precedent over results. When the Hundred launched in 2021, not a single coach was English. The late Shane Warne was chosen by London Spirit; experienced international coaches like Andy Flower, Darren Lehmann and Gary Kirsten were signed; the two emerging coaches were New Zealander Daniel Vettori and Australian Simon Katich.

Key is part of a shifting cricket culture that places names over deeds and achievements abroad over ones here.

The last six County Championship titles have been claimed by teams with English coaches: Moores (Nottinghamshire), Gareth Batty (Surrey), Mark Robinson (Warwickshire) and Anthony McGrath (Yorkshire).

If we do not have confidence in our own production line, why should we expect others to? Work abroad has been limited: Silverwood and Paul Farbrace (both Sri Lanka), Bob Woolmer (Pakistan) and Jonathan Trott (Afghanistan) rare examples of those to have taken head coach jobs of Test-playing nations this century.

Vikram Solanki is the only Englishman to move from a county position to one at the Indian Premier League, as director of cricket at Gujarat Titans. Moores was the only English coach at the Big Bash League last winter.

However, there is evidence of a shift. Ian Bell has been on coaching staffs at both tournaments. Others have ventured to the BBL to gain experience through observational or backroom roles. Andrew Gale, formerly of Yorkshire, is making big waves as a coach with Tasmania and was promoted to work with Australia A last winter.

Peter Moores is one of few English coaches able to have the privilege of calling themselves England Test coach this century

But like his compatriot Chris Silverwood, Moores lost more Test matches than he won

Foreigners appear to be judged through a different prism. For all of Fleming’s widely acknowledged man-management skills, tactical acumen and calm, calculated persona, he has never won a trophy without MS Dhoni as his captain.

Marcus Trescothick, meanwhile, failed to make the shortlist this time despite four years of experience under McCullum in which his one major failing was insisting there had been no talk of the dangers of driving on the up after first Test defeat in Perth, in keeping with the regime’s off-the-cuff policy.

Trescothick did a sound job as McCullum’s stand-in on the limited-overs tour of the Caribbean two years ago, coming home with a rare series win over West Indies, and will step up again against Pakistan.

He has been produced by a country with a revered coaching system that has launched several individuals on the road to international head coach jobs around the world.

Australia coach Andrew McDonald completed his coaching badges by the age of 27, cutting his teeth here seven years later, starting at the bottom of the pile with a Leicestershire side that had gone winless for two seasons while continue to play back in his homeland.

In improving the midlands club’s finishing positions in both the 2015 and 2016 seasons, he established a reputation as one of the brightest young coaches on the global circuit, something he gave further credence to when in his first senior coaching position in Australia he marked his debut campaign of 2016-17 by taking Victoria to the Sheffield Shield title.

At Grace Road, McDonald could put into play his belief in a hands-off approach, making players take greater responsibility and use his own previous struggles with the mental side of the sport to liberate the thinking of a team previously suffocated by struggle.

The fierce loyalty he has developed towards players was arguably forged through witnessing a group of low achievers rise above their stations with the right backing.

The art of managing people, he says, is what he invested in most as a coach. A six-month season that barely pauses for breath allows the time to get to know the individuals concerned. It gave him a steep learning curve.

Ottis Gibson won the Twenty20 World Cup with West Indies, defeated both Australia and India in Test series while in charge of South Africa and was England’s bowling coach on two occasions, having gone through the ECB coaching programme in the first decade of this century.

Gibson was mentored by an Australian Troy Cooley, but both were very much part of the English system.

Another Australian Jason Gillespie was exposed to the pressure of ending Yorkshire’s trophy drought as a young coach fresh from a maiden stint in Zimbabwe, and responded by delivering back-to-back Championships in 2014-15. Like Gibson, he moved onto the international scene, albeit briefly, with Pakistan.

Others are grateful for what the county system offers. Perhaps it’s time for us to be so too.

Sports.title: Club at centre of 'Clicky Ponting' scandal hit by fresh 'cheating' claims as umpire releases footage of ANOTHER player seemingly clicking fingers
Sports.content:
A fresh controversy has engulfed the amateur cricket club at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating scandal after an umpire released footage appearing to show another player deploying the same tactic.

Saltburn Cricket Club has been at the centre of a storm after fielder Brian Devine allegedly cheated during a Second XI Division Two match against Norton. Video footage of Devine appearing to be clicking his fingers to mimic the sound of a bat edge, tricking the umpire into giving the batsman out, went viral on social media.

On Monday, the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League launched an investigation into Devine, 38, who has since been suspended by the club for the 'foreseeable future'.

Now, fresh footage has emerged appearing to show another Saltburn player successfully using the same tactic during a Third XI match against Marton.

The fielder appears to click his fingers as the ball flies past the bat and into the wicketkeeper's gloves, prompting the on-field umpire to give the batsman out. The footage was posted on social media by Berkshire-based umpire Andy Smy.

The captain of another team in the same league earlier this week claimed the alleged tactic had not been confined to Saltburn's victory over Norton.

Saltburn have been widely condemned on social media following multiple videos emerging

He said: 'It was not confined to just one game. I was at the other end when one of our players was dismissed and I heard a big sound as the ball went through and immediately thought: "He's out."

'The umpire didn't hesitate either, but our batsman was adamant he was nowhere near the ball and couldn't understand the loud click.

'In all we had three batsmen given out caught behind, but all of them said they hadn't touched the ball. One protested so much the umpire had to speak to him and threaten him with a warning.

'I know of at least three other teams who now have suspicions and it should be noted that in one match against Shildon their wicketkeeper took eight catches.

'You hear of all kinds of things going on in cricket but this is something I haven't heard of before. I hope the league takes appropriate action.'

Earlier this week, Saltburn's Second XI forfeited their match against Marton, dumping themselves out of a cup competition, with a source close to the league saying 'none of the players will have wanted anything to do with this game while they're under such focus'.

They did, however, return to the field on Saturday for a league match against Marton, where table-toppers Saltburn crashed to a nine-wicket defeat. With Devine no longer fielding at slip, Marton chased down their target of 101 in just 20 overs.

Amateur cricket player Brian Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it appear that a batter has been caught behind when in fact they haven't hit the ball at all

Devine has been dubbed as 'Clicky Ponting' on social media for his alleged actions on the cricket field

Saltburn player has been caught on camera seeming to be clicking his fingers

And Devine, a father and auction mart worker from Guisborough, North Yorkshire, is planning to 'lie low' until the scandal dies down.

A friend said: 'Brian is completely bewildered by the way this has gone all around the world.

'He's had an Australian podcast offering to pay his legal bills today - it's the first he's heard that he's got any legal bills and he's hoping it won't get that far.

'His mates have been telling him to sell his story in Australia, but he just wants it all to go away and hopes he can get back to playing cricket, though at the moment that feels impossible.

'He woke up on Monday morning thinking the world was still the same place he'd left it the night before and suddenly his story was all over the world - in Australia, India, New Zealand and the UK, of course.

'He understands why there is an investigation but the reaction from around the world has knocked him sideways.'

The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League said it was treating the allegations of cheating 'with the utmost seriousness' and called for the 'rights of all parties' to be respected amid intense scrutiny on social media.

'We would want to place on record our genuine concern for the welfare of those at Saltburn Cricket Club and ask for all to take that into account. There are many people at the club and one of our aims will be to provide them with any wellbeing support we can,' the league said.

'Whilst we understand, to some degree, the interest this issue has generated in the press and media, it is imperative that, now this process is under way, the rights of all parties are observed, including the overriding principles of natural justice and the right to a fair hearing for any individual or entity concerned.

'Anything less risks prejudicing any formal action which may follow.'

Saltburn, in a statement on Wednesday, said: 'This has been a very distressing and stressful experience for all those concerned, and we would ask that this reality is borne in mind and that personal boundaries are respected, as we are an amateur club run entirely by volunteers.'

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal will be 'very ambitious' in the transfer market with club refusing to give up on sensational Vinicius Jr deal
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta would not be drawn on questions about Arsenal's interest in Vinicius Junior, but he did insist the champions were ‘very ambitious’ and ‘won’t sit still’ in the summer market.

The 26-year-old winger has been heavily linked with a move to north London as Arteta looks to bolster his frontline.

Vinicius’ contract at Real Madrid expires next summer and the Gunners are interested in signing the player.

Just days after Arteta said that new signings are needed to take Arsenal to a ‘different dimension’, he doubled down on his assertions.

When asked about whether more signings are expected in light of the Vinicius reports, Arteta said following Arsenal’s 4-1 pre-season victory over Girona: ‘Well we are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear.

‘We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else.

Vinicius’ contract at Real Madrid expires next summer and the Gunners are interested in signing the 26-year-old Brazilian winger

‘And you can just see it. The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing - we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do.

‘The margins are very small. And because we want to get better and the level is going to increase, we need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don't have in the team, to have bigger margins. And that's the way we have to think.’

Max Dowman shone with a goal and an assist in the match, issuing a reminder ahead of what could be an important season for the 16-year-old.

‘That's what we want,’ added Arteta. 'When you play for Arsenal, the expectations should be high and should be expecting really good things.

'We know what he's (Dowman) capable of doing. We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver.

‘But I think today he had a really good game.’

Sports.title: Dominant Josh Kerr powers to gold in the mile race at Commonwealth Games - two weeks after shattering world record
Sports.content:
It felt like the ghosts of 1954 were chasing Josh Kerr down the home straight of the Scotstoun track. Stories from the famous battle between Sir Roger Bannister and John Landy pumped nostalgia into every step of this Miracle Mile.

Queen Elizabeth II was just two years into her reign for that epic clash in Vancouver. Her great grandchildren were in the crowd for this one, braving the Glaswegian chill to watch Kerr push and shove his way to gold.

More than seven decades have passed since Bannister's victory but Kerr's spirit when he made his move in the final lap would survive the test of time. The Scotsman was boxed in with 400 metres to go, before he shoved Kenya's Brian Komen out of the way and charged from the middle of the pack.

This is the place where Kerr set personal bests in the shot put and high jump as a schoolboy. He watched his brother play rugby here for Edinburgh and, at times, this race had the physicality of a Scottish scrum.

'Welcome the world champion and the world record holder,' blasted the stadium announcer. As if this race did not have enough storylines to it, the stadium announcer was the father of fellow Scot Jake Wightman, who finished sixth.

Like Kerr, Wightman knows this place well. Both raced here for Edinburgh Athletics Club as juniors. Wightman is renowned for his sprint finish but he could not catch Kerr, who turned his bedroom into an altitude chamber to increase his lung capacity for moments like this.

Scotland's Josh Kerr surged clear of the field to claim a dominant gold medal in the mile event

There was even more anticipation for this race than when Usain Bolt stepped onto the Glasgow track for the relay in 2014. Hometown heroes, champions, record holders, Olympians were all in the mix. This was a world-class field.

Two weeks ago, Kerr broke the mile record at London Stadium. Bannister and Landy did the same before Vancouver, famously breaching the four-minute barrier for the first time.

They did not have the same footwear as the Scotsman, whose running spikes were engineered in a laboratory in Seattle.

'It definitely felt a little bit overkill - like driving a formula one car along the street for a cup of coffee,' said Kerr after his heat on Thursday.

To the untrained eye, they look like trainers that are missing the heel. Their 'rocking' midsole is designed to maximise the energy return on every stride. They were formulated to break the world record at London Stadium, where Kerr had smooth pacemakers and the shelter of ginormous stands.

Championship racing is different. The racers constantly changed pace as they jostled for position - with Botswana's Thesipo Masalela setting the pace in the opening lap.

Gusts of wind rip through Scotstoun, whipping up the 74 Commonwealth flags behind the finish line. The heatwave in the south of England, it is safe to say, did not make its way to Glasgow.

Kerr's face has greeted every commuter arriving into Glasgow, his image looming large on the billboards outside Central Station. He slicked back his hair before the starting gun, having had a fresh trim a few hours before the race. He knew this was his moment to shine.

'This is absolutely incredible,' he said. 'Doing it in front of the Scottish crowd where I learned how to race. I came here week after week as a kid. I didn't waste any energy. I knew the opportunity would open up and I had enough energy to put a gap on them in the last few hundred. I went early to save everyone some stress.

'With the World Indoors and going after the record in London, this was the one we had circled on the calendar before any of that.

'I didn't put together my performance I wanted in Birmingham 2022. I think a British crowd deserved more from me – I owed them that for sure.

No Scotsman has been named BBC Sports Personality of the Year since Andy Murray in 2016. The bookies had Kerr as joint favourite with Jude Bellingham to be named sports personality of the year before this race. This victory may well nudge the odds in his favour.

Interest in middle distance racing has waned over the years. Seb Coe, Steve Ovett, and Steve Cram enjoyed a golden era in the 1980s. This race felt like a resurrection.

Sports.title: Boxer Lee Reeves rushed to hospital after KO loss to Gary Cully as Frank Warren issues statement
Sports.content:
Boxer Lee Reeves rushed to hospital after KO loss to Gary Cully as Frank Warren issues statement

Lee Reeves had to be taken to hospital in Dublin on Saturday night as Gary Cully knocked him out to claim the BUI Celtic super-lightweight title

View 3 Images Gary Culley (left) after knocking down Lee Reeves (Image: Damien Eagers/PA Wire)

Irish boxer Lee Reeves was rushed to hospital after being knocked out by compatriot Gary Cully. The pair were fighting for the BUI Celtic super-lightweight title on the Mark Chamberlain vs Pierce O'Leary undercard.

‌



Dublin's 3Arena played host to Queensberry Promotions' No Turning Back on Saturday evening, with the main event resulting in Chamberlain snatching the IBO super-lightweight world championship from opponent O'Leary.

‌



But those who arrived for the undercard witnessed Reeves and Cully contest a breathless battle. Reeves, the clear underdog, applied pressure early on and heading into the later rounds, appeared to be on top.

‌



However, in the tenth, with both fighters tiring, he walked onto a heavy left hand from Cully and was immediately knocked unconscious. He received medical attention on the canvas and was transported directly to a local Dublin hospital for precautionary care and treatment. Promoter Frank Warren released a statement after the fight.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Anthony Joshua told exactly how he can beat Tyson Fury READ MORE :

"All our thoughts and prayers are with Lee Reeves and his family at this time as he remains in hospital," Queensberry promoter Warren wrote on social media after the event.

‌



"Everyone at Queensberry is thinking of him and we're in constant contact with his team regarding his condition as we hope for positive news."

View 3 Images Gary Culley celebrates his win (Image: Damien Eagers/PA Wire)

Cully, who captured the title, had to witness his opponent receive oxygen in the ring before being stretchered out of the arena. He, too, relayed some well wishes.

‌



"My prayers and thoughts are with Lee Reeves. Hopefully he's okay," said Cully. "He came in there as a big underdog after fighting relatively at a lower level up until now, but he really showed that he can operate at a higher level. Huge credit to him."

He acknowledged he was forced to the brink during the clash, in which he had a point deducted in the fifth round after his gumshield came out for a fifth occasion. He said: "It doesn't come into your mind when you're in there because I'm a fighter, I've always been a fighter and that's just what I do but I did have to dig deep in there.

View 3 Images Warren issued a statement (Image: Getty)

‌



"I really had to think in there and that shot that came in the tenth round was a well-timed shot. I had to stay switched on and stay concentrated. The keyword for this camp was concentration."

This bout marked Cully's second fight at super-lightweight following his move up from 135 lbs. He admits he feels much better competing at this higher weight class.

"It just brings a lot more enjoyment to my boxing, it makes me work a lot harder and I think it's shown in my last two fights," he added. "I had to dig deep in there tonight. If I had to go to the well at 135 in there, I don't know if I would have had it in me. I've found a new lease of life at this weight and now I'm ready to push on."

Sports.title: Oscar Pistorius' new life out of prison – Back in sport, job secured, living in mansion
Sports.content:
Oscar Pistorius' new life out of prison – Back in sport, job secured, living in mansion

Oscar Pistorius was released from prison in 2024, having been convicted of murdering his girlfriend, Reeva Steenkamp, 13 years ago

View 2 Images Oscar Pistorius was convicted of murder in 2015 (Image: Charlie Shoemaker, Getty Images)

Oscar Pistorius has returned to the world of sport after his release from prison. The South African Paralympic champion was found guilty of murdering his girlfriend, Reeva Steenkamp, 13 years ago, after an appeals court overturned an initial verdict of manslaughter.

‌



Upon his release from prison in 2024, Pistorius has since built a new life away from the public eye. While he was banned from competing in the Commonwealth Games as a result of his conviction, it appears as though the six-time Paralympic gold medallist has since turned his focus to other sports.

‌



As per the Daily Mail, the 39-year-old plays padel at his local court, and has also entered Ironmen events under an alias. It is said that Pistorius came 55th in a 70-mile cycling event in Durban last year.

‌



Oscar Pistorious' new lover is double of tragic Reeva Steenkamp he shot dead READ MORE :

Meanwhile, in the 'physically challenged' category, the double leg amputee came third. Beyond his sporting pursuits, the report states that Pistorius has secured employment with a sound engineering firm.

He remains living in a mansion named Bateleur, alongside his uncle, Arnold, amongst the wealthiest individuals in the area.

Arnold brought up Pistorius from the age of 15.

‌



The property is reported to feature a swimming pool and a gym enabling the former Paralympian to maintain his fitness.

Sports.title: 'I was F1 team-mates with Michael Schumacher and Lewis Hamilton – one is greatest of all time'
Sports.content:
'I was F1 team-mates with Michael Schumacher and Lewis Hamilton – one is greatest of all time'

Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher share the record for the most Drivers' Championships, having competed against one another on numerous occasions

View 2 Images Nico Rosberg claims Lewis Hamilton is F1's GOAT (Image: Clive Mason/Getty Images)

Nico Rosberg believes Lewis Hamilton is the greatest-ever Formula 1 driver, even after competing alongside the iconic Michael Schumacher. The 41-year-old raced with Schumacher between 2010 and 2012 as he made a comeback to the track with Mercedes.

‌



Hamilton replaced the German when he retired for good, and his hugely successful career on the track ever since has kick-started a debate as to which of the two drivers has made the biggest impact on the sport. Rosberg spent two extra years with the British driver and has followed his career since he left F1 in 2016.

‌



The ex-Mercedes star spoke to Sky Sports Germany after the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix as he watched Hamilton soar to his record-extending 106th career win. This was the Brit's first win since he joined Ferrari in 2025 and Rosberg had nothing but praise for his former teammate.

‌



He said: "This is a fantastic day for the sport. It’s historic. He’s the greatest of all time. It’s great that he turned things around, because last year looked so dark and bleak.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Race cancelled just 24 hours after F1 confirm addition to calendar as statement released READ MORE :

"He was practically on his way home, could have said at any moment: I’m quitting. But he persevered, now feels comfortable in the car, and you can see a positive momentum everywhere."

‌



Presenter Peter Hardenacke noted that Rosberg made this huge statement while standing next to Michael's brother, Ralf Schumacher. After it was pointed out, the 41-year-old joked that he was merely trying to create a wedge between the two pundits.

Ralf previously claimed that Hamilton would never reach his brother's heights, stating that the German was "light years" ahead of the Brit. Discussing his sibling's legacy on Formel1.de’s YouTube channel, Ralf said: "I have to say quite honestly and not because he is my brother, maybe Max [Verstappen] can change that in his career if he really continues driving like this, but for me, it’s always what Michael brought with him.

View 2 Images Who is better - Hamilton or Schumacher? (Image: Glenn Dunbar/LAT Images)

‌



"There’s no one else like him; Lewis Hamilton will never come within light years, not from my point of view."

Schumacher won five straight titles with Ferrari in the early 2000s and competed with the likes of Ayrton Senna, Damon HIll, Sebastian Vettel and Fernando Alonso. Meanwhile, Hamilton's success came after he departed McLaren in 2012 when he won four consecutive championships from 2017 to 2020.

The Brit saw Max Verstappen stop his dominant run and he slowly fell out of title contention through the early 2020s. However, Hamilton is now just 50 points behind current F1 leader Kimi Antonelli and may fancy his chances at a record-breaking eighth title.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson convinced Arsenal fan to snub Gunners for Man Utd in transfer U-turn
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson convinced Arsenal fan to snub Gunners for Man Utd in transfer U-turn

Manchester United have battled with plenty of Premier League sides for transfers over the years

View 2 Images Chris Smalling joined Manchester United after speaking with Sir Alex Ferguson (Image: Matthew Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Sir Alex Ferguson convinced Chris Smalling to abandon his dream to play for Arsenal and join Manchester United instead. The defender grew up a fan of the Gunners and was sure he would join his beloved club from Fulham.

‌



The north London outfit were in talks with the Cottagers as Arsene Wenger's reputation for developing rising stars interested Smalling. However, Sir Alex jumped in with a pitch that the centre-half just couldn't turn down.

‌



He told The Athletic: "In my head, I was going to Arsenal. Then Manchester United got in touch. I was leaving the team bus at Blackburn away and [Fulham boss] Roy Hodgson said, 'We’ve accepted a bid from Man United.' That threw me.

‌



"I felt there were more opportunities to play at Arsenal, but I spoke to Fergie and he said, 'I wouldn’t sign you if I didn’t think you could play games.' Maybe his aura felt right, but I made the right decision because I was soon playing alongside great players and winning the league."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd get fresh Benjamin Sesko injury update after star missed pre-season friendlies READ MORE :

Fergie's words stuck with Smalling and he joined United for an initial fee of around £8million, which rose to £12m due to appearance and performance bonuses. This was a major success story for a defender who had been playing non-league football just two years before his move to Old Trafford.

‌



Smalling had been at Maidstone in 2008 and ended up at Fulham, who were paying him just £5,000-a-week. He quadrupled his salary by joining United but his former non-league side didn't receive a penny, as he was a non-contract player when he departed the Stones.

Arsenal had met Fulham's clause of £10m before United swooped in, but Sir Alex's words alone convinced Smalling to ignore the allure of Wenger and head to Manchester instead. The Arsenal snub proved a wise decision for Smalling, as he would go on to win two Premier League titles and the Europa League with United.

View 2 Images Sir Alex Ferguson's 'aura' had Smalling convinced (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

‌



The defender also won numerous domestic cups and came runner-up in the Champions League final in his first year at Old Trafford. Smalling made 323 appearances for United over a decade, scoring 18 goals and assisting three times.

He joined Roma on loan for the 2019/20 season and became the first English player to score at least two goals in the same Serie A campaign since fellow United alumni David Beckham.

The centre-half joined the Italian outfit permanently for a fee of £17m and spent four years there before moving on to Al-Fayha. Smalling is now 36 years old and without a club, though he hasn't announced plans of retirement yet.

Sports.title: Man Utd’s dream final month of transfer window: £85m midfielder joins and three deals done
Sports.content:
Man Utd’s dream final month of transfer window: £85m midfielder joins and three deals done

Manchester United could make multiple dream signings before transfer deadline day on September 1

View 3 Images Michael Carrick will likely be busy in August (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have secured several new signings but Michael Carrick's team remain busy in the transfer market. As August arrives, the club have one month remaining to restructure their squad.

‌



The middle of the park remains a priority, despite signing Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. United have been linked with numerous possibilities but the manager may seek to deliver a marquee name in midfield to underline the club's aspirations to challenge for major honours next season.

‌



In attack, Benjamin Sesko requires competition, with striker Joshua Zirkzee among several players who could depart Old Trafford this summer. Meanwhile, United could begin long-term planning by testing Newcastle's determination over left-back Lewis Hall. Here, Mirror Football examines what a dream end to the transfer window might look like for the club.

‌



£85m midfielder signs

Aurelien Tchouameni arriving from Real Madrid would mark a statement signing for United in the final weeks of the window. The Red Devils refused to pay astronomical sums for the likes of Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes earlier in the summer but splashing out on Tchouameni would emphasise the club's ambitions.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The 26-year-old would represent an ideal signing for Carrick's revamped midfield as the United manager reshapes his squad following Casemiro's departure. Spanish publication AS previously reported that Real Madrid would seek around £85m for Tchouameni after the France international recently penned a contract extension with Los Blancos.

‌



Man Utd open to offers for four more players as Michael Carrick wields transfer axe READ MORE :

However, the Spanish heavyweights are keen on Manchester City's Rodri, which could prompt Tchouameni to weigh up his options elsewhere. It would provide Carrick with an impressive selection of midfielders, with Tielemans, Santos and Kobbie Mainoo all competing for spots in the United starting XI.

Lewis Hall deal

United are interested in Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall and, in an ideal scenario, would secure Luke Shaw's long-term replacement this summer. The 21-year-old has caught the eye during his spell with the Magpies, who have already demonstrated a readiness to offload key assets through the departures of Anthony Gordon and Tonali.

The England international is reportedly open to joining Carrick's side. Yet Newcastle are believed to be hesitant about selling another prized asset, meaning United may need to fork out a substantial fee for the defender, who left Chelsea for £35m in 2023.

‌



View 3 Images Lewis Hall is reportedly open to joining Manchester United (Image: Michael Driver/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

United depended heavily on Shaw throughout last season but will have worries about the seasoned full-back staying injury-free, while Patrick Dorgu appeared more effective when deployed on the left wing. Completing a move for Hall would enable United to begin their left-back succession planning early, even if the young defender commands a substantial transfer fee.

New striker joins

Benjamin Sesko's unavailability for United's early pre-season fixtures has underlined the club's need to add a striker before the summer window closes. Joshua Zirkzee has spearheaded the attack for Carrick's team but has struggled to establish himself since his arrival from Bologna in 2024, prompting reports of a possible £30m return to Serie A.

‌



While Sesko flourished after Carrick arrived at United, it took time for the Slovenian forward to cement his place in the starting lineup. The 23-year-old is still developing and shouldn't be the club's sole senior striker as United prepare for a Champions League campaign and seek to improve upon their third-place Premier League finish.

View 3 Images Dusan Vlahovic is a free agent after leaving Juventus (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Dusan Vlahovic is among several forwards to be linked with a move to Old Trafford and could offer the perfect answer to United's dilemma. The 26-year-old is a free agent after leaving Juventus this summer, where he netted 68 goals across 168 matches.

Article continues below

An expensive, high-profile signing could potentially hinder Sesko's development under Carrick and stop him from fulfilling his true potential. However, the former RB Leipzig star would benefit from competing alongside Vlahovic, who would equally be afforded the chance to impress as a rotation option at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star

Liverpool round-up as Bradley Barcola negotiations take a turn in the Reds' favour

View 3 Images Liverpool's interest in Bradley Barcola remains strong (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool's transfer window has been quieter than many fans had hoped so far. But it may be about to stir into life as negotiations with Paris Saint-Germain over long-running target Bradley Barcola continue.

‌



Pre-season has been promising with wins over Sunderland and Wrexham. Next up on the tour of the United States is a meeting with Leeds United at Chicago's Soldier Field.

‌



New signings Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz are yet to figure. The former is getting closer to his Reds debut following a shoulder injury, while Spain World Cup winner Munoz is coming to the end of his post-tournament break.

‌



It's the interest in Barcola that continues to take centre stage, with movement elsewhere in the transfer market strengthening the Reds' hand. Here's a round-up of the latest Liverpool transfer news.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Barcola replacements found

PSG are close to landing two wingers in a clear sign they are preparing for life after Barcola. They have reportedly opened talks with Ajax about signing Mika Godts for £51million.

‌



Yan Diomande transfer twist as surprise update emerges on Real Madrid target READ MORE :

Liverpool news: Green light given for huge transfer offer as talks for new signing begin READ MORE :

Meanwhile, the Champions League holders are on the verge of signing Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco for around £43m. With Desire Doue, Ibrahim Maye and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia already at the club, the position is set to become even more crowded.

Something needs to give, and that 'something' is Barcola. Liverpool have no intention of meeting PSG's £145m asking price but negotiations are continuing and the impending arrival of Godts and Akliouche should strengthen their hand.

The French champions still stand to make an enormous profit on a player who arrived from Lyon for less than £40m three years ago.

‌



View 3 Images Bradley Barcola's PSG exit has moved closer (Image: Anne-Christine POUJOULAT / AFP via Getty Images)

New Jones offer

Inter Milan are willing to increase their offer for midfielder Curtis Jones. The Serie A champions have already brought John Stones to the club this summer and are keen to add another England international, having already had one bid of around £21m rejected.

As reported by the Liverpool Echo, Inter are preparing a bid of £30m, although that is still short of the Reds' £35m valuation for the 25-year-old, who has a year left on his contract.

‌



View 3 Images Curtis Jones is attracting interest (Image: 2026 Liverpool FC)

Intermediaries working on behalf of Inter have now contacted Liverpool once more and have informed them of the Serie A side's willingness to up their offer. Jones has made 228 appearances since his debut in January 2019 but has struggled for regular first-team football.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Transfer 'approved' as £70m target 'open' to Old Trafford switch
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Transfer 'approved' as £70m target 'open' to Old Trafford switch

It's been a busy summer for Manchester United - and their transfer business looks far from over, with a number of targets still on their radar

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is looking to make a few more signings this summer (Image: Getty)

Manchester United have wasted little time getting to work this summer - but their rebuild is far from complete. With the 2026/27 campaign fast approaching, the priority is to maintain the momentum generated at the end of last season and ensure Michael Carrick's side are equipped to hit the ground running.

‌



Having spent the previous two summer windows addressing issues in attack and defence, the focus has now shifted towards strengthening the midfield. United have already made significant moves in that department, with Andrey Santos arriving from Chelsea in a £50million deal and Youri Tielemans joining from Aston Villa for £35m.

‌



However, the business is not expected to stop there. The club remain active in the market and continue to monitor a number of high-profile targets, including reinforcements beyond midfield as they look to complete a much-needed squad overhaul.

‌



With plenty still to unfold before the window closes, here are the latest Manchester United transfer headlines.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed READ MORE :

Man Utd 'internally approve' Hall transfer

Lewis Hall has emerged as a top target for United this summer, with reports claiming an official approach for the Newcastle defender has been approved internally. The England international has been linked with a move away from St James' Park for some time, with United among a number of Premier League heavyweights keeping a close eye on his situation.

‌



The Red Devils see Hall as a potential long-term replacement for Luke Shaw and are reportedly considering an opening bid worth around £60m for the 21-year-old. Although Hall remains tied down to Newcastle until 2029, the significant upheaval at the club could potentially open the door to an exit.

View 3 Images Lewis Hall is high on Man United's wish list (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

The Magpies have already seen Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe all leave in recent weeks, while Bruno Guimaraes is expected to follow suit in the coming days. Hall could yet follow them through the exit door, although Newcastle's impressive summer sales could actually strengthen their negotiating position.

‌



Having already generated around £170m through player departures - a figure that could rise towards £250m if Guimaraes completes his proposed switch to Arsenal - Newcastle are under no financial pressure to cash in on Hall.

Scott 'open to Man Utd move'

Manchester United could be set to make their third major midfield signing of the summer, with Bournemouth star Alex Scott reportedly open to the possibility of joining Carrick's side. The 22-year-old is attracting significant interest from across the Premier League, with Liverpool, Chelsea and Arsenal also keeping tabs on his situation.

View 3 Images Bournemouth's Alex Scott is reportedly open to a move to Manchester United (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

‌



Scott is believed to be considering all options at this stage, with no clear frontrunner emerging in the race for his signature. Reports claim Chelsea recently saw a £64m offer rejected by Bournemouth, although that does not necessarily put them ahead of their rivals in what remains a fiercely contested transfer battle.

The Cherries are thought to value Scott at around £70m, but given the level of competition for his services, that asking price could climb closer to £80m. United would then need to weigh up whether such a sizeable outlay represents good value.

The Red Devils remain keen to add another central midfielder after their pursuit of Atalanta star Ederson collapsed, but their recent recruitment strategy has typically focused on more measured, cost-effective deals rather than marquee spending.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Vinicius Jr transfer trick set to be repeated as next three signings lined up
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Vinicius Jr transfer trick set to be repeated as next three signings lined up

Mikel Arteta and Arsenal are eyeing three more first-team additions

View 3 Images Arsenal are hoping to land Vinicius Junior (Image: Getty )

Arsenal have seemingly kicked into life as we enter the final month of the summer transfer window. Mikel Arteta’s men faced Girona in a pre-season friendly on Saturday evening - but the focus was mainly on the club's activity off the field.

‌



That’s because the Gunners have been closely linked with several big-name targets in recent days, including Vinicius Junior of Real Madrid. The Los Blancos superstar would represent the first genuinely marquee addition of the window for sporting director Andrea Berta, having been given the green light financially to bring in the forward.

‌



Until now, Berta has only signed Piero Hincapie on a permanent basis for £34.5million, third-choice goalkeeper Illan Meslier and £34m Leandro Trossard replacement Christos Tzolis. Ahead of the transfer window’s closure on September 1, Mirror Football brings you the latest news from the Emirates Stadium.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Three signings lined up

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes is reportedly close to being signed (Image: Getty )

Arsenal are reportedly eyeing three more signings this summer. The Athletic reported on Saturday that Vinicius is Arteta’s top transfer target to strengthen the attack.

‌



An agreement between the Brazilian and Arsenal is expected to be found on personal terms if Real Madrid don’t match his demands and the forward opts not to renew at the Bernabeu. The report adds that, whether Vinicius signs or not, the north Londoners will bring in a new winger before the window shuts.

Arsenal will also seek a new midfielder, understood to be Bruno Guimaraes, after reportedly agreeing a £77m deal with Newcastle. Finally, The Athletic states a central defender is being pursued in an effort to cover the injured William Saliba in the coming months.

Vinicius transfer trick repeat

View 3 Images Ferran Torres is on Arsenal's radar (Image: FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The transfer links with Vinicius seemingly came out of nowhere last weekend. Yet, Berta is understood to have kept an eye on the 26-year-old winger’s contract situation for some time before making his approach, having seen Vinicius enter the final year of his deal.

Now, Arsenal are reportedly considering employing a similar method in their pursuit of another forward - Barcelona’s Ferran Torres - who is also due to become a free agent next summer, as it stands.

Spanish outlet Estadio Deportivo claims the Gunners have enquired about the Spain striker, who scored the decisive goal in the World Cup final last month. Barcelona want to extend Torres' contract, which is due to expire in June next year.

Article continues below

But negotiations are yet to produce an agreement, increasing pressure on Barcelona to cash in rather than risk losing the 26-year-old for nothing next summer. That, similarly to the Vinicius situation, plays directly into Arsenal’s hands as they can offer a lower transfer fee. Torres can play on either wing or through the middle, with his versatility making this potential signing an alluring one.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
