World.title: FAAN probes MMIA Terminal 2 fire scare, restores operations
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

Normal operations have resumed at Terminal 2 of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, MMIA, Lagos, as the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, investigates a fire scare after preliminary findings showed there was no actual fire at the facility.

It was earlier reported that a fire incident had occurred at Terminal 2, with FAAN stating that there were no casualties.

Providing an update on the development, FAAN’s Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Mr Henry Agbebire, disclosed that the smoke observed in the affected area resulted from the discharge of the terminal’s FM-200 fire suppression system.

Agbebire, in the statement, said the reason for the activation of the fire suppression system was being investigated, adding that normal operations had resumed at the terminal.

The statement reads: “Further to our earlier advisory regarding the incident at Terminal 2 of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, FAAN wishes to provide the following update.

“Preliminary findings indicate that there was no fire at the terminal. The smoke observed within the affected area resulted from the discharge of the terminal’s FM-200 fire suppression system. The reason for the activation of the fire suppression system is currently being investigated.

“Normal operations have since resumed at the terminal, while detailed investigations are ongoing to determine the exact cause of the incident.

“FAAN appreciates the understanding and cooperation of passengers, airlines, airport users and all stakeholders, and reiterates its commitment to the safety and security of all airport operations.”

World.title: Arteta sends transfer message amid Arsenal’s links with Vinicius Junior
World.content:
(FILES) Arsenal’s Spanish manager Mikel Arteta smiles as he applauds the fans following the English Premier League football match between Arsenal and Burnley at the Emirates Stadium in London on May 18, 2026. Arsenal ended a 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions on May 19, 2026, after Manchester City were held 1-1 in their match against Bournemouth. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP)

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has reiterated the club’s ambition in the transfer market amid growing speculation linking the Gunners with Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior.

The Brazilian international has been heavily linked with a move to the Emirates Stadium, with reports suggesting Arsenal are keeping a close eye on his contract situation at the Spanish club as they seek to bolster their attacking options.

Arteta addressed the speculation after Arsenal’s commanding 4-1 victory over Girona in a pre-season friendly. While refusing to comment directly on Vinicius, the Spaniard made it clear that the North London club remain active in the market and are determined to strengthen the squad before the new season.

“Well we are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That’s clear,” Arteta said.

“We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else.

“And you can just see it. The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing – we won’t sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do.

“The margins are very small. And because we want to get better and the level is going to increase, we need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don’t have in the team, to have bigger margins. And that’s the way we have to think.”

Arteta’s comments are expected to fuel further speculation over Arsenal’s transfer plans as the club continues to pursue reinforcements ahead of the new campaign.

The Gunners have been linked with several high-profile players this summer, with Vinicius among the biggest names reportedly on their radar should an opportunity arise.

World.title: Clashes end between Ethiopia and Tigray rebels
World.content:
Fighting has ended between the Ethiopian army and Tigray rebels, local and security sources told AFP on Sunday, after violence flared near the border with Sudan.

“There is a de-escalation,” one member of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) said on condition of anonymity, without giving any casualty figures.

Clashes involving heavy artillery and drones broke out in Shererina at about 6:00 am (0300 GMT) on Saturday and ended at about 5:00 am, they added.

A security source, who also asked for their name not to be used, confirmed that fighting had stopped.

On Saturday, the TPLF, which has been removed from the list of political parties but remains influential in the region, accused the federal authorities of having “intensified its destructive actions and taken them to a higher level”.

It also denounced what it said was a “large-scale infantry offensive.

There was no immediate response from the federal authorities.

AFP has not been able to independently verify the TPLF claims or identify which forces were on the ground in Shererina.

Fighting has been taking place in the contested area of western Tigray, which is controlled by nationalists from the neighbouring regional state of Amhara.

Federal troops and Tigrayan forces have for several months been massed along the border of northern Tigray in the north of Ethiopia, with both sides accusing the other of wanting to trigger a new conflict.

Fears of a new war have grown as a result, less than four years after the end of a bloody conflict between the two sides, with the TPLF backed by local militias and the Eritrean army.

It left at least 600,000 dead, according to an African Union estimate.
