World.title: Teachers, NGO call for more emphasis on global education in school curricula
World.content:
NGO Mondo has said Estonia's education system should place greater emphasis on global citizenship, and the chair of the Estonian History and Civics Teachers' Association agrees. The Ministry of Education says that global education competencies are already included in the current curricula.

Global education, knowledge of how global issues affect the daily lives of individuals, communities and society, and how everyone can influence the world, has been promoted in Estonia for 15 years.

Schools can choose elective courses, take part in themed weeks and projects, and such content has been integrated into various subjects, but according to those involved, this has been done in a fragmented way.

Meelis Niine, project manager at the non-profit organization Mondo, told ERR that in the future global education could be described more clearly in the general sections of the national curricula and in subject syllabi, and that global citizenship competencies could also be set out more specifically.

"If there were a separate emphasis specifically on global citizenship competencies, it would help make global education a clearer and more integral part of formal education. What do I mean by global citizenship competencies? On the one hand, it means that young people should understand different global challenges, their local dimension, and how global challenges are reflected locally. At the same time, it is also important to care about these issues and to take active action," he said.

Niine thinks this is a weak point because many young people in Estonia may be fairly well informed about global issues, but they make relatively few active choices in their daily lives or engage in civic activism.

Madli-Maria Naulainen, chair of the Estonian History and Civics Teachers' Association, said that global education is certainly already part of civics classes, but that does not mean it could not receive greater emphasis.

"At the moment, a great deal depends on the individual teacher – some choose to address these topics more, others less," Naulainen explained. "I very much agree that the topic of global education should be highlighted more and should not depend solely on teachers' individual choices."

According to the chair, the association has worked closely with Mondo all along and has helped distribute the educational materials created by Mondo for use in civics lessons.

"That line of cooperation certainly exists now, but in a situation where teachers can choose which topics they use to achieve particular learning outcomes, a specific section in the curriculum would provide a better guarantee that everyone has gained some knowledge in this area," Naulainen argued.

Ministry: Schools have a lot of autonomy

Adviser on general education policy at the Ministry of Education and Research, Mare Oja, said there is no contradiction in the current situation. The principles of global education are already included in the national curriculum's general competencies and core values.

"We have universal human and social values, which include both solidarity, civic engagement and seeing oneself as a citizen of the world. In Estonia, the national curriculum is a general document on the basis of which schools develop their own curricula, and our schools have a great deal of autonomy," she said.

She added that in upper secondary school, 63 of the 96 courses are determined by the national curriculum, while schools design the remaining third themselves, creating their own profile and deciding what they want to explore in greater depth. Some focus on economics education, others on financial literacy, and some on global education. As a result, the situation is diverse.

"In fact, all these principles are already included. Specific topics are covered in geography and civics. For example, when we talk about cultural diversity, foreign languages, language and literature, and certainly history all support that," Oja said.

Teachers: Schools may lack broader perspective

Madli-Maria Naulainen of the History and Civics Teachers' Association noted that although several school subjects touch on global education, what may be lacking is a broader perspective that would help students understand globalization and give them an idea of what development cooperation is and why it is necessary.

"In today's globalized world, it is inevitable that we must keep up with these issues. Understanding and solidarity toward others are also areas that could certainly be better addressed through these topics," Naulainen said.

Maari Ross, adviser at the Humanitarian Aid Bureau of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said some European countries also look to Estonia's education system for inspiration, but at the same time, the issue of fragmentation still needs to be addressed.

"One important area is regional support and cooperation networks. In Estonia, we actually have several very strong schools and competence centers working on global education. The question is how to ensure and improve the sharing of their experience with others. Another important area is research and evaluating the impact of global education – how to increase the interest of Estonian researchers in studying global education," Ross said.

According to Naulainen, civics is expected to provide good citizenship education, while in reality the subject has a fairly limited place in schools.

"Civics as a subject is taught only in the sixth, ninth and 12th grades. We have discussed whether the volume of civics education should perhaps be expanded, because expectations have increased and there are visible signs of polarization and extremism in society," the association's chair said.

At the end of last year, stakeholders in the field produced a vision document, and on that basis they are now moving toward drafting an action plan.

World.title: Chevron CFO bullish on Iraq after West Qurna 2, Nassiriya agreements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chevron boasts “significant potential” to expand its activities in Iraq over the next decade, according to Chief Financial Officer Eimear Bonner, highlighting the US oil company’s increasing trust in the country’s energy sector after recent deals with Baghdad.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Bonner said that Iraq remained one of Chevron’s top priority markets for future production expansion after the signing of preliminary agreements to pursue negotiations on the massive West Qurna 2 and Nassiriya oil fields.

She added that Chevron has been encouraged by its interaction with Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Iraq’s Ministry of Oil while discussions continue and that the corporation is also collaborating with Baghdad on diverse crude export routes to boost Iraq’s long-term energy security.

The statements bolster rising trust among foreign energy corporations after Al-Zaidi’s visit to the United States earlier this month, during which Iraq inked more than $60 billion in investment deals covering energy, infrastructure, banking, and technology.

World.title: Syria joins Saudi Arabia, Jordan in warning Iraq over Iran-backed militias
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Syria has joined Saudi Arabia and Jordan in warning Baghdad that strikes conducted from Iraqi soil against neighboring nations may result in military strikes against the armed groups responsible, according to Syrian military officials cited by regional media.

According to Al Jazeera and the US-funded Al Hurra, a senior Syrian military source said that Damascus will react to any strikes from Iraq by attacking the “terrorist militias” involved inside Iraqi territory.

The purported warning comes amid a steep increase in regional tensions after US-Saudi bombings against Iran-backed militias in Iraq in retaliation for drone assaults on Saudi oil installations, which Riyadh said were conducted from Iraqi territory.

The Iraqi government has frequently said that it would not allow Iraqi land to be used as a launchpad for attacks on neighboring nations.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi recently issued an order establishing a comprehensive security strategy aimed at enhancing state authority and preventing armed organizations from endangering regional security.

The new threat puts further pressure on Baghdad, as more neighboring nations indicate they may take direct action if cross-border assaults continue.

Iraqi authorities have attempted to prevent such a situation, claiming that security activities should be overseen by the Iraqi government rather than foreign forces.

Several Iran-backed organizations operating inside Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) are at the heart of the conflict, including Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada.

While the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security system, some of its sections have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and have been accused by regional governments of carrying out strikes outside of Baghdad’s jurisdiction.

For Iraq, the diplomatic stakes go beyond security.

Baghdad has been attempting to reestablish ties with Syria as part of greater regional economic integration, including talks on resurrecting the old Iraq-Syria oil pipeline to the Mediterranean, which is considered strategically crucial for diversifying Iraq’s export routes outside the Gulf.

The purported Syrian warning comes at a critical moment for Al-Zaidi’s administration, which has spent recent months bolstering relations with Washington, Ankara, Riyadh, and Damascus while portraying Iraq as a secure destination for global investment.

The mounting threats from neighboring Arab governments highlight the importance of Baghdad demonstrating its ability to prevent armed groups from conducting strikes independent of the state.

Failure to do so risks increasing regional military tensions and jeopardizing Iraq’s aspirations to boost commerce, energy cooperation, and infrastructure projects with its neighbors.

The Syrian government has not issued an official warning, and IraqiNews.com has not independently confirmed the statements ascribed to the Syrian military source.

However, the claims reflect rising regional worry that strikes by Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi soil could further destabilize the area and hamper Iraq’s diplomatic and economic goals.

World.title: Iran-backed militias threaten Iraq’s ties with US and Gulf
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Escalating tensions between Iran-backed militias are providing one of the most serious hurdles yet to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s ambitions to deepen ties with the United States and Gulf states while luring billions of dollars in international investment.

The most recent crisis followed US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq, when Saudi Arabia accused militias operating from Iraqi territory of firing drones at oil installations in the kingdom’s Eastern Province.

Riyadh claimed that the operation targeted the militias responsible for the assaults rather than the Iraqi state or its military forces, but Baghdad denounced the strikes as a breach of national sovereignty.

The recent tensions are being fueled by numerous prominent Iran-aligned organizations operating inside Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), notably Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada.

While the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security apparatus, many of its groups have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and have occasionally conducted operations outside of Baghdad’s chain of command.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi responded by calling an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security, canceling a planned trip to Saudi Arabia, and announcing a comprehensive security strategy to prevent Iraqi territory from being used to launch attacks on neighboring countries.

The administration also reiterated its resolve to keep all weapons entirely under state control.

That vow has gained importance after Al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington earlier this month, during which Iraq and the United States reiterated their commitment to completing the US-led coalition operation by the end of September 2026.

During the visit, Al-Zaidi pledged to ensure that all weapons eventually come into the control of the Iraqi state, citing it as a cornerstone of his government’s security strategy and a crucial step toward bolstering Iraq’s sovereignty and stability.

Since entering office, Al-Zaidi has maintained a policy of balancing Iraq’s ties with rival regional and international forces.

During recent travels to Washington, Ankara, and Tehran, he achieved huge investment and cooperation deals totaling tens of billions of dollars in the energy, banking, technology, infrastructure, and industrial sectors.

His administration has also attempted to strengthen connections with Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Turkey, and other Gulf nations via new transportation corridors, energy alliances, and trade agreements aimed at diversifying Iraq’s economy beyond oil and positioning the country as a regional center linking the Gulf to Europe.

According to analysts, Baghdad’s approach is highly dependent on proving that the Iraqi state, rather than armed groups, controls the country’s security and foreign policy.

Continued strikes from Iraqi territory risk eroding the country’s reputation with major regional allies and international investors, at a time when foreign investment has risen after years of turmoil.

The stakes rose when US President Donald Trump said that recent US-Saudi operations against Iran-backed militias were coordinated with the Iraqi government, a claim Baghdad has denied.

Observers believe it reflects rising discontent among Iraq’s leadership with armed groups accused of dragging the nation into regional conflicts that contradict Baghdad’s diplomatic and economic interests.

Al-Zaidi is currently facing the most significant test of his leadership.

Delivering on his promise to place all weapons under state control will be critical not only for Iraq’s internal security but also for maintaining trust with the United States, Gulf Arab states, and international investors, many of whom support many of the country’s largest economic projects.

Baghdad’s dilemma now extends beyond managing ties between Washington and Tehran.

It demonstrates that the Iraqi state possesses both the authority and the political will to prevent Iran-backed militias from using Iraqi territory to launch attacks that risk isolating the country, harming relations with Arab neighbors and the United States, and jeopardizing Iraq’s long-term economic recovery and investment goals.

World.title: Iraq faces growing fiscal strain
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is under increasing financial strain as plummeting oil earnings tighten government budgets, with Health Minister Abdul Hussein al-Mousawi saying that ensuring monthly public-sector wages has become the government’s top priority.

Speaking at a public meeting, al-Mousawi stated that the government requires approximately 10.8 trillion Iraqi dinars ($8.2 billion) per month to pay public-sector salaries, while current monthly oil revenues have fallen to approximately 2.5 trillion dinars, highlighting the growing gap between government obligations and income.

The statements are one of the most direct public acknowledgements by a top Iraqi official of the government’s financial challenges after months of decreased oil prices and fewer export profits.

Iraq’s government finances remain very vulnerable to variations in global energy markets because the vast bulk of public revenue comes from crude oil.

Official figures published this week indicated that oil accounted for over 84% of federal income in the first five months of 2026, but collections decreased by more than one-third compared to the same time the previous year as oil prices and export profits plummeted.

The health minister also warned of financing restrictions in the healthcare sector, citing worries about the supply of medications and the government’s capacity to sustain public services if financial pressures continue.

The fresh warnings follow weeks of increased regional tensions, which disrupted oil markets and added uncertainty to Iraq’s economic prospects.

As OPEC’s second-largest producer, Iraq relies on oil exports to fund wages, pensions, social welfare, and the majority of government expenditure, making the budget susceptible to long-term reductions in crude prices.

Economists have long cautioned that Iraq’s reliance on oil income makes the nation susceptible to external shocks, while a hefty public-sector pay bill constrains the government’s budgetary flexibility.

Previous administrations attempted to diversify income streams via tax changes and non-oil investments, but hydrocarbons remain the economy’s backbone.

The financial pressure comes at a critical time for Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s government, which has been promoting Iraq as a destination for billions of dollars in foreign investment following agreements signed with US, Turkish, and international companies in energy, banking, technology, and infrastructure.

Continued budgetary strain may make it more urgent to accelerate economic reforms, raise non-oil income, and improve public financial management to lessen Iraq’s reliance on petroleum exports.

They also emphasize that preserving investor trust will be contingent on the government’s ability to maintain macroeconomic stability while continuing to fund big development projects.

Despite the present issues, Iraq has large foreign currency reserves, which act as a financial cushion for the government.

However, experts warn that while reserves might help absorb short-term shocks, they are not a substitute for the fundamental changes needed to diversify the economy and reduce its dependence on unpredictable oil earnings.

World.title: Iraq expects record 22 million pilgrims for Arbaeen
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is prepared to welcome around 22 million pilgrims for this year’s Arbaeen pilgrimage, including up to 5 million overseas tourists, in what officials believe to be one of the country’s greatest religious gatherings and a significant boost to tourism and the local economy.

According to Iraqi official data, well over 22 million people are anticipated to attend the annual pilgrimage to the holy city of Karbala, with 4.5 million to 5 million pilgrims coming from outside Iraq.

The government has announced that tens of thousands of volunteers would be deployed to assist pilgrims, and Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has urged officials to boost the number of buses and other transport services to facilitate travel during the festival.

The surge of foreign tourists is projected to have a substantial impact on Iraq’s tourism, hospitality, transportation, and retail industries, with hotels, restaurants, transit operators, and local businesses benefitting from increased demand during the pilgrimage season.

Officials have extended transportation networks in preparation for this year’s pilgrimage, including more rail services, buses, and logistical assistance, as part of larger measures to boost connectivity and promote Iraq’s tourist industry.

The government has increasingly highlighted religious tourism as a crucial pillar of economic diversification, with millions of people visiting the country’s holy sites at Karbala, Najaf, Kadhimiya, and Samarra each year.

According to officials, continuing investment in infrastructure and tourist services will help Iraq become one of the Middle East’s major religious tourism destinations, while also creating jobs and helping local economies around the country.

World.title: Reports: Iraq PM threatened to resign over militia disarmament
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has threatened to resign if Iran-aligned armed groups do not cooperate with his government’s efforts to bring all weapons under state control, according to reports citing political sources, highlighting the growing pressure on Baghdad to address one of its most difficult security challenges.

According to sources, Al-Zaidi warned leaders of Iraq’s Shi’ite Coordination Framework that if armed groups did not react to government efforts to disarm and completely submit to state authority, he would stand down.

IraqiNews.com was unable to independently verify the claims, and the Prime Minister’s office had no immediate response.

According to the sources, Al-Zaidi has been more dissatisfied by what he sees as a lack of cooperation on one of his administration’s fundamental commitments: guaranteeing that all weapons stay solely under the control of the Iraqi government.

The claims came days after US-Saudi airstrikes struck Iran-backed groups in Iraq in response to drone assaults on Saudi oil installations, which Riyadh said were launched from Iraqi territory.

The bombings forced Al-Zaidi to call an emergency security conference, cancel a planned trip to Saudi Arabia, and unveil a new security strategy aimed at preventing Iraqi territory from being used to launch attacks on neighboring nations.

Armed organizations have emerged as one of Al-Zaidi’s most pressing problems.

Since entering office, he has attempted to solicit billions of dollars in foreign investment with trips to Washington, Tehran, and Ankara, while portraying Iraq as a stable location for oil, infrastructure, and technological projects.

Analysts believe Baghdad’s economic objectives are strongly dependent on its ability to show that the state, not armed groups, controls Iraq’s security strategy.

Repeated strikes conducted from Iraqi territory have strained ties with regional allies and risk weakening investor trust.

According to Western diplomatic sources published by Asharq Al-Awsat, key Iraqi officials, including Al-Zaidi and members of Iraq’s security apparatus, have received threats in connection with the government’s attempts to restrict weaponry outside of state control.

Unlike many regional leaders, Iraq’s prime minister leads by wide political agreement rather than a legislative majority, restricting his power to make unilateral choices.

Major security and political changes usually need agreement among Iraq’s different political blocs.

Al-Zaidi’s biggest power may not be the threat of resignation, but rather the international backing his administration has garnered as a result of recent accords with the United States, Turkey, and other allies.

These agreements, which span energy, finance, technology, and infrastructure, have boosted hopes that Iraq will attract tens of billions of dollars in investment if security improves.

Whether Al-Zaidi can translate that international momentum into domestic reforms will ultimately depend on gaining broader political support for his pledge to keep all weapons under Iraqi state control, which has become one of his government’s most closely watched tests.

World.title: Iraq denies launching strikes from its territory against neighboring nations
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The military spokesperson for the Iraqi commander-in-chief, Sabah al-Numan, confirmed on Thursday that neither a foreign nor local body has presented proof that recent regional drone attacks were launched from Iraqi territory.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), al-Numan urged accusing parties to submit reliable proof, saying that Baghdad has yet to receive such data.

The development comes following statements made by the Saudi Ministry of Defense, alleging that drone attacks targeting key oil infrastructure in the past few days originated in Iraq.

The Iraqi official indicated that the government will neither tolerate unilateral military acts from within its borders nor accept foreign violations of its territorial sovereignty.

Al-Numan’s remarks come a day after the United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated airstrikes targeting several bases of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), killing and injuring many fighters.

The joint operation targeted several logistical and weapons storage locations in different provinces in Iraq, escalating the current regional battle.

The PMF described the joint US-Saudi strike as a dangerous escalation and a clear breach of Iraqi sovereignty.

World.title: Iraqi oil flows to continue via Turkey’s Ceyhan as renewal deal is discussed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish sources told Reuters that crude oil shipments from northern Iraq to the Turkish port of Ceyhan will continue while the two countries seek an arrangement to extend the pipeline’s operation for another 12 months.

On July 27, a bilateral agreement that had been in place for decades ended. Despite expectations, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi did not sign a 12-month renewal deal during his meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Tuesday.

According to a Turkish official, oil flows via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline, which is Baghdad’s only operational export pipeline, will continue while negotiations for a renewal deal are still in progress.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar recently announced a 12-month extension agreement between the two countries.

During a joint press conference in Ankara, Erdogan stated on Tuesday that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement as soon as possible.

An extension is intended to provide additional time for discussions on a complete accord. Turkey aims to fully utilize the 1.5 million barrels per day pipeline and consider expanding it to oil fields in southern Iraq.

Turkish data suggests that the pipeline currently transports approximately 170,000 barrels per day.

World.title: Quote of the day by Selena Gomez: You have to be uncomfortable sometimes in order to move forward
World.content:
You have to be uncomfortable sometimes in order to move forward

That quote perfectly captures the outlook of Selena Gomez, one of the world's most influential pop stars and a prominent advocate for mental health awareness.

Throughout her career, Gomez has spoken openly about embracing uncertainty, confronting personal struggles and accepting that growth often comes through life's most challenging moments.

Born in Grand Prairie, Texas, on July 22, 1992, Selena Gomez is an American singer, actress, producer and entrepreneur. Over the past two decades, she has evolved from a Disney Channel star into a global entertainment icon, earning recognition not only for her music and acting but also for her advocacy for mental health and emotional well-being.

How Selena Gomez became a global icon

Gomez first gained prominence as Alex Russo in the Disney Channel series Wizards of Waverly Place. She later established herself as a successful recording artist with hit songs including Come & Get It, Good for You, Lose You to Love Me and Calm Down. Alongside her music career, she has appeared in films and television projects while producing the acclaimed series Only Murders in the Building.





She is also the founder of Rare Beauty, a cosmetics brand that has become a major global success.

Beyond entertainment, Gomez has become one of the most influential voices on mental health. She has spoken publicly about living with lupus, undergoing a kidney transplant, and dealing with anxiety, depression and bipolar disorder. Through interviews, documentaries and the Rare Impact Fund, she has consistently encouraged people to seek professional help, prioritise emotional well-being and challenge the stigma surrounding mental illness.

Her quote, "You have to be uncomfortable sometimes in order to move forward," reflects the philosophy that has guided much of her personal and professional journey.

What the quote means

Rather than viewing discomfort as something to avoid, Gomez presents it as an essential part of growth. Every major life transitionâstarting a new career, overcoming failure, recovering from personal setbacks or embracing changeârequires stepping into unfamiliar territory.

While those moments may feel uncertain or intimidating, they often become the foundation for learning and self-improvement.

The quote also aligns with a widely accepted principle in psychology. Personal development rarely occurs when people remain within familiar routines. Taking on new responsibilities, facing difficult conversations or challenging long-held fears can build resilience, confidence and emotional maturity.

Temporary discomfort, when approached with the right mindset, often leads to long-term progress.

Gomez has repeatedly demonstrated this belief throughout her career. She has taken creative risks by experimenting with different musical styles, transitioning into film production and launching successful business ventures. At the same time, she has been candid about taking breaks from the spotlight to focus on her physical and mental health, showing that moving forward sometimes also means recognising when to pause, recover and return stronger.

Ultimately, Selena Gomez's words serve as a reminder that discomfort is not necessarily a sign of failure. More often, it is evidence that a person is growing, adapting and moving closer to becoming the best version of themselves. In a world that often celebrates instant success, her message encourages people to embrace uncertainty, trust the process and keep moving forward.

World.title: 'He will not be taken back': Mayawati expels former MP Ashok Siddharth from BSP again
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) president Mayawati on Sunday announced the expulsion of former Rajya Sabha member Ashok Siddarth from the party, less than a year after

him in September 2025.

Mayawati said Siddarth had been expelled with immediate effect in the interest of the party and its movement, adding that he would not be re-inducted in the future.

"In the interest of the party and the movement, Ashok Siddarth has been expelled from the BSP with immediate effect and will not be taken back into the party in future," the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister wrote on X.

Mayawati X post

Explaining the decision, Mayawati noted that Siddarth had earlier been expelled over "indiscipline" during the Maharashtra assembly elections, particularly over issues related to coordination with the party's state unit in ticket distribution.

Mayawati added that Siddharth was subsequently entrusted with organisational responsibilities in states outside Uttar Pradesh to help strengthen the party's base. However, despite repeated warnings, complaints of indiscipline and violation of party directives continued to surface from Karnataka, Odisha and West Bengal, she alleged.

The BSP supremo also clarified that the ex-Rajya Sabha MP had been relieved of all party responsibilities on Saturday.





She further alleged that rumours about his possible return to Uttar Pradesh were being deliberately spread to create confusion within the organisation and derail the BSP's preparations for the next Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.

from the BSP in February last year over alleged "anti-party" activities.

World.title: 'Still a student, learning every day': Rahul Gandhi's Gen Z-style Friendship Day wish
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Sunday wished people on Friendship Day with a Gen Z-style post, using the popular Korean finger heart emoji while joking that he had only just learnt its meaning.

Sharing a photo on Instagram, Rahul wrote, "Still a student, still learning something new every day. Today's lesson: it's Friendship Day and this ð«° is a heart. Happy Friendship Day, everyone. Lots of love!"

The Congress MP has increasingly tried to connect with younger audiences through social media, informal interactions and youth-focused campaigns. In recent months, he has frequently addressed students, spoken about issues such as paper leaks and unemployment and referred to 'Gen Z' in several speeches and social media posts.

He has also interacted with students in India and abroad, sharing videos of conversations on careers, anxiety, education and democracy.

During the nationwide 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' campaign, Rahul repeatedly urged young people to raise their voices over examination irregularities and recruitment issues.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

More recently, he appealed directly to Gen Z on social media over electoral issues, saying the youth would 'protect the Constitution, defend democracy and prevent vote theft'.





In another post, he advised young people that 'nothing in life is linear' and encouraged them to stay flexible and persevere.

The finger heart is a popular gesture that originated in South Korea and has become a global internet trend through K-pop, K-dramas and social media. It is made by crossing the thumb and index finger to resemble a tiny heart.

The gesture is widely used to express affection, gratitude, friendship or appreciation and has become especially popular among Gen Z users across platforms such as Instagram, WhatsApp and X.

Rahul Gandhi's use of the symbol on Friendship Day marks another attempt by the Congress leader to communicate in a style familiar to younger internet users.

World.title: Indian diaspora in China flags anti-India social media posts, visa curbs at 1st embassy outreach
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Members of the Indian diaspora in China raised concerns over anti-India content on Chinese social media, declining work visas and employment restrictions for spouses during an Open House hosted by the Indian Embassy in Beijing.

The outreach event, held on Friday, had Indian Ambassador Vikram Doraiswami and senior embassy officials interact with professionals from across sectors on issues affecting the Indian community in China.

Participants flagged what they described as a growing trend of abusive posts targeting Indians, including comments on Indian culture and food habits, besides raising concerns over the declining number of work visas being issued by Chinese authorities and difficulties faced by spouses seeking employment, reported PTI.

Addressing the gathering, Doraiswami said Chinese authorities were aware of the increase in such online content and were taking measures to curb it. He added that the embassy was responding by pushing verified, fact-based information through its official social media channels.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The ambassador also announced that documentation requirements for Chinese citizens applying for Indian visas would be eased from next week to encourage greater travel to India.





Seeking to improve support for the Indian community, the embassy is working on a legal assistance framework for professionals facing workplace-related issues in China and plans to institutionalise the Open House as a regular forum for addressing consular and community concerns.

Doraiswami also said the mission would expand cultural outreach programmes, including events such as the Vasant Mela, to promote India's cultural diversity and cuisine.

The interaction comes amid efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to stabilise bilateral relations, with Doraiswami, who assumed charge in May, stepping up diplomatic engagement with Chinese officials.

World.title: 'Drugs part of enemy nations' terror plan to hurt India': PM Modi during 'Nasha Mukt Yuva' launch - top quotes
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday launched the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan', calling on the country's youth to stay physically and mentally fit and remain away from drug abuse.

He said achieving the goal of a developed India requires a healthy, confident and drug-free younger generation. During his address, PM Modi also highlighed how the drugs affect one's family and career.

Launching the campaign through video conferencing, PM Modi said the initiative is not only for individuals, families and society but also for the nation. He added that the next 100 Sundays would represent 100 strong steps towards a drug-free India.

"Next 100 Sundays will mark 100 strong steps towards drug-free India," he said.

PM Modi also warned that drug trafficking was part of a larger strategy by hostile forces to weaken India and called for greater public vigilance. "Hurting India's interests by supplying drugs part of enemy nations' terror plan," he said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Here are the top quotes from his address:

Youth must stay fit for developed India

"Today, all countrymen have come together for a great and important resolve. The campaign we are witnessing is meant for individuals, families and society, but above all, it is for the nation. The campaign, 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat', clearly reflects this resolve. As the country moves towards the goal of a developed India, it is essential that our youth remain physically and mentally healthy and stay away from drugs and other such harmful substances."

"The campaign we are witnessing today is for the individual, the family, and society; above all, it is for the nation. The very name of this movementâthe 'Drug-Free Youth' initiative under the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan â clarifies its resolve. As the nation sets its sights on becoming a Viksit Bharat, it is essential that our youth be healthy in body and mind, brimming with self-confidence, and forever free from the deadly habit of drugs. This is the objective of the campaign... This campaign was launched last year as a pilot project from Kashi... Over 125 spiritual organizations have joined us today for the welfare of crores of our fellow citizens."

"By being addiction-free, you need to protect your potential. You need to be aware that drugs get you high for a short time, but take your career and family to a new low/bottom.

From Varanasi to nationwide campaign

"As the MP from Kashi, I am happy that this campaign was launched last year from the sacred land of Kashi as a pilot project. Along with scientific clarity, it also carries spiritual energy. Social organisations and NGOs have joined this initiative for the welfare of crores of Indians. Together, they have prepared a roadmap through the Kashi Declaration. Today, we are witnessing how the welfare-oriented idea that emerged from Kashi has become a national project. From today, the Nasha Mukt Yuva campaign is being launched across the country."

"The 'Nasha Mukta Yuva Abhiyaan' is launching across the country today... There is immense power in collective action, and today, driven by that very strength, this campaign is set to touch the heart of every young person. Lakhs of youths across the nation took a pledge to stay free from drugs... The pledge taken today will continue to move forward steadily over the next hundred weeks."

"Drug use disturbs focus, takes you away from dreams. If a youth gets addicted to drugs, his aspirations take a hit, family gets shattered."

Govt's anti-drug drive and national campaign

"Today, the government stands firmly with the youth in the campaign against drugs. Strict action is being taken in the country against drug traffickers and drug abuse; there have been many times more arrests compared to before, and drugs worth thousands of crores of rupees have been seized. This shows how tough our government is against drugs."

"Today, thousands of students from schools, colleges and universities are connected online to this programme. Even lakhs of volunteers of MY Bharat are also connected. The NSS jawans too have joined us. People from different sectors, institutions and backgrounds--more than 1 crore youths are together today. I congratulate all of you for this big movement."

Youth key to Viksit Bharat, drugs part of enemy agenda

"You are India's Amrit Peedhi. You will shape your lives over the next 20-25 years, and you will lead the country to the goal of a Viksit Bharat in 2047, and you will be at the helm. You will be the ones to reap its full benefits."

"The country needs your energy, your imagination, and your talent, so staying drug-free is crucial for the country and for your own lives."

"When a young person falls prey to drug addiction, it is not just that individual who loses; a dream is lost. Hostile nations conspire and leave no stone unturned to drag our youth into the trap of addiction. Profiting from the supply of drugs while aiming to destroy a country like ours is part of their terror-driven agenda."

Parents, teachers and society must lead the fight

"We must always keep this in mind: if any child from our home has become a victim of addiction, do not hide it under the guise of social prestige. Seek help from whoever is needed."

"Make efforts to free your child from addiction with medical help."

"We should also foster a culture of open communication with children in the family, so that you can hold their hand before they get caught in such a whirlpool."

"Along with teaching the courses, please also discuss the dangers of drugs with the students. Launch a movement against addiction on your campus. Your efforts can bring big results."

"The support of society, the power of yoga and meditation--these strengthen our inner resolve against addiction. And today, we also have facilities like rehabilitation centres to help quit drugs."

"I appeal to all of you that you are all the leaders of this great movement. You have further strengthened my belief that the youth of India is so aware, so sensible, and so serious about their duties."

The 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan' aims to encourage young people to stay away from substance abuse and become ambassadors of positive social change in their communities.





The launch marks the beginning of a 100-week nationwide Jan Bhagidari campaign, under which awareness programmes will be organised every Sunday across the country.

Activities will include sports events, walkathons, meditation sessions, cultural programmes, street plays, discussions, art competitions and community engagement initiatives.

The campaign brings together educational institutions, youth organisations, civil society groups, industry bodies and more than 125 spiritual organisations to build a collective movement against substance abuse.

Youth from over 10,000 locations across the country are participating through schools, colleges, universities, MY Bharat volunteers, NSS volunteers, youth clubs, NGOs and industry associations.

World.title: 'Dismantle terror infrastructure first': India's US envoy hits out at Pakistan over Indus Waters Treaty
World.content:
Indiaâs envoy to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra said Pakistan had eroded the foundation of the

over the past five decades. He added that Islamabad had âdismantledâ the goodwill and friendship that underpinned the 1960 agreement, and that New Delhiâs decision to keep the treaty in abeyance merely acknowledged that reality.

As reported by US' Newsweek magazine, Kwatra said the treatyâs preamble reflected a commitment made 'in a spirit of goodwill and friendship', but Pakistanâs conduct had weakened that foundation over half a century.

âIt is worth remembering that the treaty's preamble declares it was concluded âin a spirit of goodwill and friendshipâ. Pakistan spent half a century dismantling that goodwill and friendship. The abeyance merely acknowledges what Pakistan's conduct had already destroyed,â Kwatra said.

His remarks came after Pakistan recently hosted a conference protesting Indiaâs decision to keep the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance on April 23 last year, a day after Pakistan-trained terrorists killed 26 people in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir.

The IWT, signed by India and Pakistan in 1960, divided the waters of the six rivers of the Indus basin between the two countries. India was given control over the eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej which account for about 20 per cent of the basinâs water, while Pakistan received rights over the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab carrying around 80 per cent.





âThat asymmetry stifled development for decades in Indian regions that could have benefited from better water rights. India honoured the treaty anyway,â Kwatra said according to Newsweek.

The envoy said Pakistanâs approach towards India had been marked by wars, hostility and cross-border terrorism, citing the 1965, 1971 and 1999 conflicts along with major terror attacks, including the 2001 Parliament attack, the 2008 Mumbai attacks, the 2016 Uri and Pathankot attacks, the 2019 Pulwama attack and the 2025 Pahalgam attack.

Kwatra also said that if Pakistan sincerely wanted Indiaâs cooperation on bilateral issues, it must first dismantle the terror infrastructure it has built over the years.

On implementation of the treaty, Kwatra alleged that Pakistan had repeatedly delayed Indian projects and opposed efforts to revisit the agreement in view of changing technology and requirements.

âPakistan also consistently blocked India's initiatives to renegotiate the treaty in light of six decades of technological change, which would have let India develop its hydropower potential,â Kwatra added.

âBit by bit, Pakistan eroded India's faith that it could exercise its rights under the treaty, or hope for a better one suited to today's realities,â he said.

Responding to calls for India and Pakistan to resume talks, Kwatra said past initiatives had failed to address core concerns.

Water and blood cannot flow together',â Kwatra said.

Kwatra also said Pakistan should focus on improving its own water management instead of blaming India for its challenges.

"The Government of Pakistan would do better to fix its dismal water productivity, than to stage conferences blaming India and issuing threats,â he said, adding, âThe habit of pinning every domestic failure on India has grown old."

World.title: Culture can slow ageing, says study
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Want to age more slowly? The answer may lie not just in exercise and diet, but also in a trip to the theatre, museum or even the cinema.

A new study by Japanese researchers has found that older adults who engage more frequently in cultural activities tend to have a lower physiological ageâa measure of how well the body's organs and systems are functioningâthan their actual age, suggesting cultural engagement may be an overlooked tool for healthy ageing.

Researchers from the Institute of Science Tokyo analysed 4,207 observations from 1,899 adults aged 50 years and above in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. Participants who more frequently visited cinemas, museums, art galleries, theatres, concerts or the opera had lower physiological age. Every one-point increase in cultural engagement score was associated with a 0.085-year reduction in physiological age, even after adjusting for income, health status, employment, smoking, physical activity and other factors.

The association persisted in a four-year follow-up analysis. Physiological age, estimated using 10 markers including blood pressure, lung function, grip strength, walking speed, BMI, haemoglobin, cholesterol and blood sugar, is considered a better predictor of disease and mortality than chronological age.

The researchers said cultural engagement may promote healthy ageing by strengthening social connections, reducing loneliness and stress, improving mental well-being and encouraging healthier lifestyles.





Indian experts said the findings reinforce the importance of staying socially engaged as people age.

Dr Prasun Chatterjee, Group Clinical Lead, Department of Geriatric Medicine and Longevity Sciences, Apollo Hospitals, and former professor at AIIMS, said the findings reinforce that healthy ageing depends not only on diet and exercise but also on social and cultural engagement. Social interaction improves memory and mood by boosting serotonin and dopamine, enhancing emotional well-being, memory and a sense of purpose, which encourage healthier lifestyles.

In the Indian context, he said, activities such as visiting parks, cinemas, theatres or places of worship can provide similar benefits by promoting happiness, social connection and purpose.

Prof Rajesh Sagar, psychiatrist at AIIMS, New Delhi, said social and cultural engagement promotes healthy ageing by strengthening emotional support networks, improving cognitive function and reducing chronic stress.

World.title: Global breastfeeding rates rise, India yet to arrest decline
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Even as exclusive breastfeeding rates have improved globally over the past decade, India continues to lag behind, with the proportion of infants exclusively breastfed for the first six months declining from 63.7% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) to 55.8% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).

Ahead of World Breastfeeding Week (August 1-7), the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF called for stronger support systems for mothers, saying global exclusive breastfeeding has increased from about 37% in 2012 to over 47% today, driven by sustained investments in health systems, community counselling and maternity protection. However, the agencies said progress remains uneven and many countries continue to fall short of global targets.

Responding to a question in the Rajya Sabha, the Union health ministry attributed the decline in India's exclusive breastfeeding rate to multiple factors, including socio-cultural practices, family customs, individual preferences, the use of pre-lacteal feeds and infant milk substitutes, and breastfeeding frequency.

The ministry, however, highlighted improvements in other breastfeeding indicators.





Early initiation of breastfeeding within one hour of birth increased from 41.8% to 50.1%, while the proportion of infants below six months receiving any breast milk rose marginally from 95.1% to 95.6%.

The Rajya Sabha question had sought to know whether the government had assessed the impact of rising Caesarean deliveries, inadequate postnatal lactation counselling and early return to work, particularly among women in the informal sector.

While the ministry did not provide findings of any such assessment, it said the National Health Mission promotes exclusive breastfeeding through the Mother Absolute Affection (MAA) programme, lactation management centres, healthcare worker training, Poshan Tracker-based counselling and community awareness campaigns.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It also cited a 2025 NITI Aayog evaluation, which found that new mothers were receiving information on exclusive breastfeeding during the postnatal period.

Calling breastfeeding one of the most effective public health interventions, WHO and UNICEF said it provides essential nutrition, protects children against infections, strengthens immunity, supports cognitive development and lowers mothers' risk of breast and ovarian cancers and type 2 diabetes. The agencies said scaling up proven interventions, including skilled breastfeeding support, community counselling, paid maternity leave, supportive workplace policies and stronger regulation of breast-milk substitute marketing, could prevent nearly 400,000 child deaths and 140,000 maternal deaths globally every year.

World.title: Gen Zers ‘reel’ in visibility for modest clothing store in Chennai
World.content:
As the Pedestrian Plaza in Pondy Bazaar wears a twilight glow, young shoppers shuffle towards a modest clothing store near ‘Crocs’ store opposite Geetha Cafe. One shopper browses the displays, eyes peeled for that perfect dress, and comes upon it, unfortunately, seconds too late. She eats her heart out watching it disappear into someone else’s ravenous shopping bag. Friends hold up outfits for each other, debate colours and designs, and leave with a heavier bag, a lighter purse and a sprightlier step. Qualms written all over her face, another shopper admits: “Here to keep a friend company while she shopped, I ended up with a shopping bag of my own. The seller’s warmth won me over.” On-the-spot reviews of this timbre do not dissipate but solidify into eWOM (electronic word of mouth), gaining permanence as reels and stories on buyers’ Instagram accounts.

Rani Collection run by Sikkander Sultan is nourished by healthy organic social media content, posted by customers on their Instagram pages impressed with its range of trendy tops for women and girls. Rani Collection operates from a small space within another store and for the convenience of its customers, a small part of it often spills on to a space under a tree without being underfoot. The sanctity of the pedestrian space is maintained. “Nearly 85 percent of our customers come through reels. Influencers visit us regularly, and that is how most of the people get to know about our shop,” he says.

Organic Instagram stories about Rani Collection put out by Gen Z customers and lifestyle vloggers https://www.instagram.com/p/DbQVifRzuEN/ https://www.instagram.com/p/DaC_mF7gxXW/ https://www.instagram.com/p/DZKbdnsge9W/ https://www.instagram.com/p/DY8qYmxx-9E/ https://www.instagram.com/p/DVivsNrDxB2/ https://www.instagram.com/p/DU0bkdnjDPC/

Gen Zers largely home in on this shop, and Sikkander is no spring chicken, being at least one generation removed. His family soaked in the garment business, Sikkander slid into the trade as effortlessly as one would through an open door, without any existential cogitations about purpose and calling. He established the shop at Pondy Bazaar in 2013, a good six years before pedestrianisation transformed the street into a congregating point, particularly for Gen Z. Sneakers-wearing Gen Zers now flitting in, in good numbers, Rani Collection could not have kept Insta visibility off its racks even if it tried to. It draws shoppers from far beyond Chennai, much of that, says Sikkander, is thanks to Instagram. The reach however is not confined to the state. After spotting the store on Instagram, a customer travelling from Kolkata stopped by during their visit to Chennai. Others have walked in from Malaysia and Sri Lanka after watching viral reels, while some families in the United Kingdom and the United States often shop through relatives visiting Chennai. Depending on the size of the order, the store also ships internationally.

Rani Collection offers trendy tops starting at ₹300 (and these include crop tops, peplum tops, corset kurtis and knot kurtis) , while complete sets are priced between ₹500 and ₹3000. Even a purchase as small as ₹300 can be exchanged, and the customer can be certain he would not be met with an irritated frown. As Sikkander puts it, “We want our customers to confidently wear what they buy. If a garment is pushed to the back of a closet, it does injustice to the tailor who carefully stitched it. Every single thread reflects their hard work. I have seen their daily struggles, and I want their work to be valued.” Beyond the bustling shop floor is a business man whose outlook is as contemporary as the collection he curates. He believes businesses must evolve with changing times, embracing new ideas and remaining relevant to a young demographic. Sikkander notes honesty and hard work are non-negotiables: open from 10:30 a.m to 10:30 p.m, seven days a week, “break” and “rest” sound like gibberish in Sikkander’s ears. Without normalising workaholism, one has to acknowledge this commitment just as one would this pavement store’s rack strength and its owner’s affability. And Gen Zers are doing that with likes, reposts and reels on Instagram.

(Street Feed is a column about the quotidian on the streets of Chennai that finds itself in the spotlight on social media because residents took to it, and in cases involving a modest enterprise, customers were so impressed with its products that they drummed up a buzz around it through reels and posts)

World.title: Iran media denies Trump claim that Tehran asked U.S. not to strike
World.content:
Iran’s Mehr news agency on Sunday (August 2, 2026) denied President Donald Trump’s claim that the Islamic republic asked the United States to refrain from conducting new strikes.

Citing military officials, the agency said the allegation “was nothing but a new lie” and that the Iranian armed forces were “on high alert and ready for any eventuality”.

On Saturday (August 1, 2026), Mr. Trump said the U.S. was “ready to go against the Islamic republic” but that Tehran and other West Asian countries had asked him to hold off on fresh strikes.

He said he had made the decision, subject to reaching a deal with Iran.

“This would include the Immediate, Complete and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran’s nuclear threat,” wrote Mr. Trump in a Truth Social post.

On Sunday (August 2, 2026), Iran’s Fars news agency, citing a source close to Iranian negotiators, said “as long as the United States maintains its hostile actions, the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed”.

Iran has blockaded Hormuz since the start of the war, requiring vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the waterway.

World.title: Kerala heavy rains LIVE: Eight dead, 13 injured, 8 missing following rains: Kerala CM
World.content:
Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan today said that eight people have died, an equal number are missing and 13 were injured in the previous day’s heavy rains, which caused property damage, landslides and waterlogging in many parts of the State.

Also read | Cloudburst-like event exposes gaps in State’s weather forecasting, disaster preparedness

In a statement issued by his office, Mr. Satheesan also said that 27 houses were completely destroyed, 196 homes were partially damaged and 5,792 people have been shifted to the 209 relief camps set up across the state.

Meanwhile,Kerala braced for the likelihood of heavy rains and flooding on Sunday (August 2, 2026), the latest in a string of stormy days that have wreaked havoc across the State.

Also read | Heavy rain in Kerala results in increase in storage level in Mullaperiyar dam; Idukki Collector cautions public to avoid night travel on ghat section

The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange alert for 12 districts. It has warned of heavy rains and the possibility of flash floods, mudslides, and road and neighbourhood inundation in Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Ernakulam, Idukki, Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur, and Kasargod districts.

World.title: Decision on declaring drought by August end, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar
World.content:
Stating that the State will decide on declaring a drought in rain-deficient regions across Karnataka by August end, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Sunday (August 2, 2026) said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has promised to meet after the Parliament session. So far, Karnataka has received 35% of the normal rainfall, he added.

Also read | Karnataka government failed to tackle drought, says H.D. Kumaraswamy; JD(S) to attend all-party meet on Cauvery crisis

Speaking to presspersons in Bengaluru, he said that the Revenue Department will have to draw a list of taluks as drought-hit based on the NDRF norms. “Ministers will provide ground report and that will be compiled by the Revenue Department based on the norms. The final assessment would be discussed in the Cabinet and then submitted to the Government. Declaring drought-hit regions will be decided by August end.”

The Chief Minister said that though catchment areas of Cauvery and its tributaries were receiving rainfall, places such as Mandya, Mysuru and Bengaluru have not received rainfall.

He said that he had appealed to Prime Minister for time, and that he has assured to provide time. “Let parliament session end and by then rain situation is expected to improve.” When asked if the Centre would come to State’s rescue and if all party delegation was considered, he said: “We are working in federal structure. For some reasons all party delegations could not be taken in the past.”

World.title: The Hindu brings the historic 1947 Independence Day edition back to life
World.content:
When India awoke to freedom on the morning of August 15, 1947, The Hindu was there to chronicle the birth of a newly independent nation. Now, as the country prepares to celebrate its 80th Independence Day, the publication is offering readers a rare opportunity to step back into that exact moment in time.

To honour this defining milestone, The Hindu has reproduced its landmark August 15, 1947, edition in its entirety. The original 32-page edition has been meticulously reproduced exactly as it appeared nearly eight decades ago.

Within its pages, readers will find rare photographs documenting the hard-fought freedom struggle and the country’s first proud steps forward. It features deeply personal Independence Day greetings from monumental figures including Jawaharlal Nehru and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

Alongside these historic messages are vivid, on-the-ground reports of the very first flag-hoisting ceremonies that swept the nation. Even the vintage s offer a fascinating, nostalgic glimpse into India’s social and commercial landscape of the era.

Starting August 1, 2026, limited copies of this collector’s edition will be available on Zepto across major Indian cities. It is a unique chance to own and hold history in your hands.
